learn.hook: Where is the furry cat hiding? Let us find her!
points: Top means the highest part. Bottom means the lowest part.
Above means higher than something. Below means lower.
Inside means within a box or room. Outside means not in it.
On means touching the top. Under means below it.

example.q: A cat sits in a basket. The basket is under a table. Where is the cat?
steps: The cat is in the basket.
So the cat is inside the basket.
The basket is under the table.
example.answer: Inside the basket, under the table

learn.reallife: Shoes go under the bed. Books go inside the bag. The fan is on top, near the ceiling.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ceiling fan is near the top of a room.
The fan hangs from the ceiling, high up.
Your feet are at the top of your body.
Feet are at the bottom. Your head is at the top.
Milk poured in a glass is inside the glass.
The milk is within the glass.
A bird flying in the sky is under the tree.
A bird high in the sky is above the tree.
Roots of a tree are below the ground.
Roots grow down into the soil.

quiz.q: Riya keeps her laddoos in a box. Where are the laddoos?
quiz.explain: She put them in the box. So they are inside it.

quiz.q: Which part of a tree is at the top?
quiz.explain: Leaves are high up on the tree. Roots are at the bottom.

quiz.q: Arjun's cat sleeps under his bed. Is the cat above or below the bed?
quiz.explain: Under means below. So the cat is below the bed.

quiz.q: A kite flies high over the house. The kite is ___ the house.
quiz.explain: High over the house means above the house.

quiz.q: Meena plays in the garden. Her mummy is in the kitchen. Who is outside the house?
quiz.explain: The garden is outside the house. The kitchen is inside.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a garden is inside the house

quiz.q: Kabir puts his bag on the chair. Where is the bag?
quiz.explain: On means resting on the top. So the bag is on top of the chair.

teach.ask: Gappu: I lost my ball! How do I tell where it is?
teach.praise: Yay! Now I can say on, under, inside or outside!
teach.nudge: Can I use words like inside, outside, top or bottom?

learn.hook: Where do muddy shoes go when we come home? Let us think!
points: We keep shoes outside the room.
Garbage goes inside the dustbin.
In the ball game, a ball in the basket is IN. A ball that misses is OUT.
A bed and a fan are inside a room. Trees and clouds are outside.

example.q: Kabir throws 3 balls. Two drop in the basket. One falls on the floor. Say IN or OUT for each.
steps: Ball 1 is in the basket: IN.
Ball 2 is in the basket: IN.
Ball 3 is on the floor: OUT.

learn.reallife: At home we leave shoes outside the door. A banana peel goes inside the dustbin.

games.title: Good habits
items: We leave muddy shoes outside the room.
A banana peel goes on the road.
Peels and wrappers go inside the dustbin.
A ball that drops in the basket is IN.
A ball that misses the basket is IN.
It is OUT. It did not go in.
The sun is outside the house.
We see the sun in the sky, outside.

quiz.q: Riya ate a toffee. Where should the wrapper go?
quiz.explain: Garbage goes inside the dustbin. That keeps our home clean.
quiz.mistake: Does not link garbage with inside the dustbin

quiz.q: Joseph comes home from the park. His shoes are muddy. Where should they go?
quiz.explain: Muddy shoes stay outside the room so the room stays clean.

quiz.q: Aisha throws a ball. It drops into the basket. What does she call out?
quiz.explain: The ball went inside the basket. So it is IN.

quiz.q: Kabir's ball misses and falls on the grass. Is it IN or OUT?
quiz.explain: The ball is not inside the basket. So it is OUT.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any throw counts as in

quiz.q: Which one is found inside a room?
quiz.explain: A bed is kept inside a room. Clouds and trees are outside.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up things inside and outside a room

quiz.q: Which one is found outside the house?
quiz.explain: The road is outside the house. So the bus is outside.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up things inside and outside a house

teach.ask: Gappu: My ball fell next to the basket. Is it IN or OUT? And where do my muddy shoes go?
teach.praise: OUT for the ball, shoes outside! Clean nest, happy Gappu!
teach.nudge: Did the ball go inside the basket? Where should dirty shoes stay?

topics.title: On the tree, under the tree

learn.hook: Who sits on the tree and who rests under it? Let us look!
points: Birds sit on the branches of a tree.
A boy resting in the shade sits under the tree.
On a face, the eyebrows are above the eyes.
The nose is above the mouth. The smile is below the nose.

example.q: Draw a face. Where do the eyebrows go? Where does the smile go?
steps: Draw the nose in the middle.
The smile goes below the nose.
example.answer: Eyebrows above the eyes, smile below the nose

learn.reallife: On a hot day, people rest under a big tree. Crows and sparrows sit on its branches.

games.title: Where does it go?
pairs: at the bottom of the face

items.text: The boy rests ___ the tree in the shade.

quiz.q: A parrot sits on a branch. Where is the parrot?
quiz.explain: A branch is part of the tree. So the parrot is on the tree.

quiz.q: Harpreet sits in the cool shade below a neem tree. Where is he?
quiz.explain: Below the tree means under the tree.

quiz.q: Where are your eyebrows?
quiz.explain: Eyebrows are just above the eyes.

quiz.q: Riya draws a smile on a face. Where should it go?
quiz.explain: The mouth is below the nose. So the smile goes there.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up above and below on a face

quiz.q: A cat sleeps in the shade. A crow sits on a branch. Who is under the tree?
quiz.explain: The cat is in the shade below the tree. The crow is on the tree.

quiz.q: Where is your nose?
quiz.explain: The nose is below the eyes and above the mouth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up above and below on a face

teach.ask: Gappu: I am drawing a face. Where do I put the eyebrows and the smile?
teach.praise: Eyebrows above, smile below. What a happy face!
teach.nudge: Is the smile higher or lower than the nose?

learn.hook: Our Tiranga waves high! Which colour is on top?
points: Our flag, the Tiranga, has three colours.
Saffron is at the top. White is in the middle. Green is at the bottom.
White is below saffron and above green.
The blue Ashoka Chakra is in the middle of the white band.
The flag is a rectangle. It has 4 corners and 4 sides.

example.q: Which colour is just below saffron in our flag?
steps: Just below it is the white band.

learn.reallife: On 15 August and 26 January we see the Tiranga at school and on buildings.

games.title: Flag from top to bottom
games.prompt: Put the colours from top to bottom

games.title: True or false?
items: Green is at the top of our flag.
Saffron is at the top. Green is at the bottom.
The Ashoka Chakra is in the middle.
It sits in the middle of the white band.
It is a rectangle. A rectangle has 4 corners.
It is a rectangle: top, bottom and two sides.

quiz.q: How many colours are there in the bands of our flag?
quiz.explain: The bands are saffron, white and green. That is 3.
steps: Saffron is 1, white is 2, green is 3.

quiz.q: Which colour is at the top of the Tiranga?
quiz.explain: Saffron is the top band.

quiz.q: Which colour is at the bottom of the Tiranga?
quiz.explain: Green is the lowest band.

quiz.q: Where is the Ashoka Chakra on the flag?
quiz.explain: The chakra is in the middle of the white band.

quiz.q: The white band is below saffron. What is below the white band?
quiz.explain: Green is below white, at the bottom.

quiz.q: Our flag is a rectangle. How many corners does it have?
quiz.explain: A rectangle has 4 corners, one at each end of the top and the bottom.
steps: Top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.
quiz.mistake: Counts the sides of a triangle

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to draw our flag. Which colour goes where?
teach.praise: Saffron top, white middle, green bottom. Jai Hind, Gappu!
teach.nudge: Which colour goes at the bottom? What sits in the middle?

learn.hook: Meow! The furry cat is hiding. Can position words find her?
points: In our song, we look for a lost cat. We use position words.
A clue tells where a thing is: on, under, inside, behind, next to.
Follow the clue and look in that place.
Give clear clues so a friend can find a hidden thing.

example.q: Clue: 'The cat is under the table, behind the basket.' Where should Meena look?
example.answer: Under the table, behind the basket

learn.reallife: When Papa cannot find his keys, a clue like 'on the shelf' helps him find them fast.

games.title: Clue and what to do
pairs: Look on top of the shelf
Look at the back of the door

games.title: Good clues
items: 'The cat is on the sofa' tells us where to look.
It names a place and a position word.
'The cat is somewhere' is a good clue.
It does not say where. Use position words.
To find a toy under the bed, we look on the bed.
Position words help us find lost things.
They tell us exactly where to look.

quiz.q: Clue: The cat is inside the cupboard. Where will you look?
quiz.explain: Inside the cupboard means we open it and look in.
quiz.mistake: Does not follow the position word in the clue

quiz.q: Arjun hid his ball under the chair. Which clue is right?
options: The ball is on the chair
The ball is in the bag
The ball is under the chair
quiz.explain: The ball is below the chair. So 'under the chair' is right.

quiz.q: Which is the best clue?
options: The pen is inside my pencil box
quiz.explain: It says the place and the position word. Easy to find!
quiz.mistake: Picks a clue that does not say where

quiz.q: The cat sits on the wall. Riya looks under the bed. Will she find it?
quiz.explain: The cat is on the wall, not under the bed. Riya is looking in the wrong place.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the position in the clue

quiz.q: Kabir says, 'The toy is behind the TV.' Where should Aisha look?
options: At the back of the TV
quiz.explain: Behind means at the back.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word behind

quiz.q: In the song, children look for a lost cat. Which words help most?
options: Number words like one and two
Position words like on and under
Colour words like red and blue
quiz.explain: On, under and inside tell where to look for the cat.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that position words tell where

teach.ask: Gappu: My red ball is lost! How can you tell me where to look?
teach.praise: A clue with a position word! I found my ball!
teach.nudge: Which word tells me the place? On? Under? Inside?

learn.hook: Is the ice cream cart near or far? Let us look!
points: Near means close to you. Far means a long way away.
Something near looks big. Something far looks small.
You have a left hand and a right hand.
In a row, we read from left to right.

example.q: In the row 🍎 🍌 🍇, which fruit is in the middle? Which is on the left?
steps: Start from the left: 🍎 is first.
🍌 is next. It is in the middle.
example.answer: 🍌 is in the middle. 🍎 is on the left.

learn.reallife: We look left and right before we cross a road. The moon is far. Your bag is near.

games.title: Near or far?
items: A plane high in the sky

items.text: In 🐶 🐱 🐭, the ___ is in the middle.
In 🚗 🚌 🚲, the ___ is on the far right.
The sun looks small because it is very ___.

quiz.q: Aisha stands next to her school bag. The bus stop is a long walk away. What is near Aisha?
quiz.explain: Next to her means close. So the bag is near.

quiz.q: Which one is far from us?
quiz.explain: The sun is very, very far away. That is why it looks small.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun is near because it is bright

quiz.q: In the row ⭐ 🌙 ☀️, what is on the far left?
quiz.explain: Start at the left end of the row. ⭐ comes first.

quiz.q: In the row 🥭 🍌 🍎 🍇, what is just right of 🍌?
quiz.explain: Find 🍌. Move one step right. You reach 🍎.

quiz.q: Harpreet sees two trains. One looks big. One looks tiny. Which train is far?
quiz.explain: Far things look smaller. So the tiny-looking train is far.

quiz.q: Five children stand in a line: Riya, Joseph, Meena, Kabir, Aisha. Who is in the middle?
quiz.explain: Two children are on each side of Meena. So Meena is in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Picks the second or fourth child

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend says the tree is far. What does far mean?
teach.praise: Super! Near is close. Far is a long way. Left and right help too!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what near and far mean? What about left and right?

topics.title: Chhuk chhuk train: before and after

learn.hook: Chhuk chhuk! Our train is here. Who is in front?
points: The engine is at the front. The bogies come after it.
Before means in front of. After means behind it in the line.
Count the bogies after the engine one by one.
In a human train, each child holds the child in front.
From a train window we see fields, rivers and bridges go by.

example.q: 🚂 🟦 🟥 🟩 🟨. How many bogies come before the 🟥 bogie?

learn.reallife: On a train trip, our coach number tells us if we are near the engine or at the back.

games.title: Line up the train
games.prompt: From the front to the back

items.text: The engine comes ___ all the bogies.
In 🚂🟦🟥, the 🟥 bogie is ___ the 🟦 bogie.
In 🚂🟩🟨🟦, the bogie just after 🟩 is ___.
A train has an engine and bogies. The ___ is at the front.

quiz.q: 🚂 🟦 🟦 🟦 🟦 🟦. How many bogies come after the engine?
quiz.explain: Count the bogies after the engine: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts the engine as a bogie

quiz.q: 🚂 🟩 🟩 🟥 🟩. How many bogies are before the 🟥 bogie?
quiz.explain: Between the engine and 🟥 there are 2 green bogies.
quiz.mistake: Counts the bogies after instead of before

quiz.q: 🚂 🟨 🟥 🟨 🟨 🟨. How many bogies are after the 🟥 bogie?
quiz.explain: After 🟥 come 🟨 🟨 🟨. That is 3.

quiz.q: Meena, Joseph and Riya make a human train. Meena is in front, then Joseph, then Riya. Who is just after Meena?
quiz.explain: Joseph holds Meena from behind. He is just after her.
quiz.mistake: Picks the last child instead of the next one

quiz.q: 🚂 ⬜ 🟥 ⬜. Colour the bogie just before 🟥 green. Which one turns green?
quiz.explain: The bogie just before 🟥 is between the engine and 🟥.

quiz.q: Kabir's train passes a bridge. After that it passes a field. What came before the field?
quiz.explain: He saw the bridge first, so the bridge came before the field.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up before and after in time

teach.ask: Gappu: In 🚂🟦🟥🟩, which bogie is before 🟥 and which is after it?
teach.praise: 🟦 before, 🟩 after! Chhuk chhuk, Gappu is happy!
teach.nudge: Which bogie is nearer the engine? That one is before.

learn.hook: Suwali spilled her buttons! How can she tidy them?
points: Sorting means putting things that are alike in one group.
Suwali sorts buttons by colour: red ones together, blue ones together.
Sorted groups are easy to count.
We can sort leaves, pebbles and buttons too.

example.q: Buttons: 🔴 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔴. Sort them by colour. How many are in each group?

learn.reallife: At home we sort clothes, spoons and socks. Shopkeepers sort fruits into baskets.

quiz.q: Suwali has 🔴🔵🔴🔴🔵. How many red buttons?
quiz.explain: Pick out the red ones: 🔴🔴🔴. That is 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the buttons, not just red

quiz.q: Which button goes in the blue group?
quiz.explain: Only 🔵 is blue.

quiz.q: Why do we sort buttons into groups?
quiz.explain: When alike things are together, we can count each group fast.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why sorting helps

quiz.q: Riya sorts leaves: 🍃🍂🍃🍂🍂. How many green leaves 🍃?
quiz.explain: Pick out the green ones: 🍃🍃. That is 2.

quiz.q: Joseph puts grey pebbles in one heap and white pebbles in another. How is he sorting?
quiz.explain: Grey and white are colours. So he sorts by colour.
quiz.mistake: Does not name the rule used for sorting

quiz.q: 🟡🟡🔵🟡🔵. Sort by colour. Which group has more?
quiz.explain: Yellow has 3. Blue has 2. Yellow has more.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have red and blue beads all mixed up. What should I do?
teach.praise: Red with red, blue with blue! Now I can count them!
teach.nudge: How do I decide which beads go together?

topics.title: Sort another way, match one to one

learn.hook: Can the same buttons be sorted in a brand new way? Yes!
points: The same buttons can be sorted again in a new way.
Sort by size: big buttons and small buttons.
Sort by holes: buttons with 2 holes and buttons with 4 holes.
Match one to one: give each cup one saucer.
If nothing is left over, both have the same number.

example.q: 4 buttons: big red, small red, big blue, small blue. Sort them by size.

learn.reallife: At lunch, we give each child one plate. If plates are left over, there are more plates than children.

quiz.q: Buttons: big 🔵, small 🔵, big 🔴. Sort by size. How many big buttons?
quiz.explain: The big ones are big 🔵 and big 🔴. That is 2.
quiz.mistake: Sorts by colour instead of size

quiz.q: Meena sorted buttons by colour. Now she sorts the same buttons by holes. Is that fine?
options: Yes, we can sort in a new way
No, only one way is allowed
quiz.explain: The same things can be sorted in many ways.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is only one way to sort

quiz.q: Which is a way to sort buttons?
options: By the day of the week
quiz.explain: Buttons can have 2 or 4 holes. We can group them that way.
quiz.mistake: Picks a rule that does not fit buttons

quiz.q: There are 4 children and 4 chairs. Each child sits on one chair. How many chairs are left?
quiz.explain: Each chair got one child. None are left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks something is always left over

quiz.q: 5 cups and 3 saucers. Put one saucer under each cup. How many cups get no saucer?
quiz.explain: 3 cups get saucers. 2 cups are left without one.

quiz.q: Arjun has 3 friends and 3 pencils. He gives each friend one pencil. What is true?
options: Same number of friends and pencils
quiz.explain: Every friend got one and none were left. So they are the same.

teach.ask: Gappu: I sorted my buttons by colour. Can I sort them another way? And how do I know if I have one cup for each saucer?
teach.praise: Sort by size or holes, and match one each. Clever!
teach.nudge: What else is different about the buttons? Is anything left over?

chapters.title: What is Long? What is Round?

learn.hook: A snake and a worm went for a walk. Who is longer?
points: Long things stretch a big way from end to end.
Short things stretch only a little way.
To compare, put both ends at the same start line.
Longest means more long than all others. Shortest means less long than all.

example.q: Riya has a pencil and a crayon. Both start at the same line. The pencil ends farther. Which is longer?
steps: Line up one end of both.

learn.reallife: A train is long. A toffee is short. A plait can be long or short.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put them from shortest to longest

games.title: True or false?
items: A train is longer than a car.
A train has many coaches. It is very long.
A spoon is longer than a bed.
A bed is much longer than a spoon.
To compare length, start both things at the same line.
Then the one that ends farther is longer.
An eraser is longer than a cricket bat.
A cricket bat is much longer.
A giraffe's neck is longer than a cat's tail.
A giraffe has a very long neck.

quiz.q: Which is longer?
quiz.explain: A cricket bat is much longer than a tiny matchstick.

quiz.q: Which is the shortest?
quiz.explain: A paper clip is the shortest of the three.
quiz.mistake: Picks the longest instead of the shortest

quiz.q: Meena's ribbon is long. Aisha's ribbon is short. Whose ribbon is longer?
quiz.explain: Long is more than short. So Meena's ribbon is longer.

quiz.q: Two sticks start at the same line. Stick A ends first. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: The stick that ends first does not go as far. So Stick A is shorter.

quiz.q: Which animal has a long trunk?
quiz.explain: Only the elephant has a trunk. It is long!
quiz.mistake: Does not know which animal has a trunk

quiz.q: Kabir lays a pen next to a ruler. The ruler is longer. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: If the ruler is longer, the pen must be shorter.
quiz.mistake: Gets confused between longer and shorter

teach.ask: Gappu: My worm and my pencil look the same. How do I know which is longer?
teach.praise: Clever! Line them up and see which goes farther!
teach.nudge: Should I put them at the same start? Which word tells me long or short?

learn.hook: A ball and a plate are at a party. Which can bounce away?
points: Round things have curved sides, like a ball.
Flat things have flat faces, like a book.
A ball is round all over. It has no flat face.
Some things have both, like a tin can. Its sides are curved. Its top is flat.

example.q: Is a dice round or flat?
steps: All its faces are flat squares.

learn.reallife: A laddoo and a ball are round. A book and a carrom board are flat.

quiz.q: Which one is round all over?
quiz.explain: A ball is curved everywhere. Books and bricks have flat faces.

quiz.q: Which one has flat faces?
quiz.explain: A dice has 6 flat faces. Oranges and marbles are round.

quiz.q: A square gift box is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A box with square faces is like a cube.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every solid is a sphere

quiz.q: A sheet of paper is flat. Which is also flat?
quiz.explain: A notebook cover is flat like the paper. A laddoo and a ball are round.

quiz.q: A tin of ghee has curved sides. What shape is it like?
quiz.explain: A tin has a curved side and two flat round ends. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all curved things are spheres

quiz.q: Joseph's birthday cap is pointy at the top. It is like a ___.
quiz.explain: A birthday cap has a round bottom and a point on top. That is a cone.

teach.ask: Gappu: I found a ball and a book. Are they the same shape?
teach.praise: Yes! A ball is round. A book is flat!
teach.nudge: Which one is round? Which one is flat?

topics.title: Round things, long things, box shapes

learn.hook: A bangle and a ladder are very different. Can you tell how?
points: Round things like a bangle or a coin go in the circle box.
Long things like a pencil or a ladder go in the long rectangle box.
A matchbox has flat faces and corners. A brick and a lunch box have the same shape.
Things with the same shape match, even if size or colour is different.

example.q: Which one has the same shape as a matchbox: a brick, a ball or a birthday cap?
steps: A matchbox has flat faces and corners.
A brick also has flat faces and corners.
A ball is round. A cap is pointy.

learn.reallife: A lunch box, a shoe box and a brick all have the matchbox shape.

quiz.q: Which thing has the same shape as a matchbox?
quiz.explain: A brick has flat faces and corners, just like a matchbox.
quiz.mistake: Does not match shapes by their faces

quiz.q: Riya draws a bangle. Which box should it go in?
quiz.explain: A bangle is round. Round things go in the circle box.

quiz.q: Kabir draws a ladder. Which box should it go in?
quiz.explain: A ladder is long. Long things go in the rectangle box.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT shaped like a box?
quiz.explain: A ball is round all over. A brick and a matchbox are box shapes.

quiz.q: Meena has a small ball and a big football. Do they have the same shape?
options: Yes, both are round like a ball
quiz.explain: Size does not change shape. Both are round all over.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different size means a different shape

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a matchbox have?
quiz.explain: Top, bottom and 4 sides. That is 6 faces.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the top and bottom faces

teach.ask: Gappu: Is a brick like a ball or like a matchbox? Where do I draw a bangle?
teach.praise: Brick like a matchbox, bangle in the circle box. Super!
teach.nudge: Does a brick have flat faces or is it round?

learn.hook: Let us build a house, a tower and a robot with things from home!
points: We can build with boxes, books, bottles, caps and funnels.
Boxes and books have flat faces. They stack well.
Balls are round all over. They roll off a stack.
A cone or a cap sits well on top, like a roof.
Tell the shapes you used: 'I used two boxes and a cap.'

example.q: Aisha builds a tower: a big box, a small box and a cone on top. Why does it stand?
steps: Boxes have flat faces. One sits flat on the other.
The cone has a flat bottom, so it sits on the box.
Its pointy top must go last.
example.answer: Flat faces stack, and the cone goes on top

learn.reallife: Builders use bricks with flat faces to make strong walls.

games.title: Builder's true or false
items: Books are good for the bottom of a tower.
A ball is good for the bottom of a tower.
It is round and rolls away.
A cone can be the roof of a toy house.
Its pointy top looks like a roof.
A box will stay on the tip of a cone.
The tip is pointed. The box will fall.
Bottle caps can be wheels of a toy bus.

quiz.q: Joseph wants a tall tower. Which is best to stack?
quiz.explain: Boxes have flat faces. They sit on each other without rolling.

quiz.q: Why does a ball fall off a stack?
quiz.explain: A ball has no flat face to sit on, so it rolls off.
quiz.mistake: Does not link round shape with rolling

quiz.q: Riya makes a toy house from a box. What can be its roof?
quiz.explain: A cone has a flat bottom and a pointy top, like a roof.
quiz.mistake: Picks a round thing that will roll off

quiz.q: Kabir makes a bus from a box. Which can be its wheels?
quiz.explain: Bottle caps are round like wheels.
quiz.mistake: Does not see which shape is like a wheel

quiz.q: Meena stacks 3 books. She puts 1 box on top. How many things are in her stack?
quiz.explain: 3 books and 1 box make 4 things.

quiz.q: Aisha says, 'My robot has a box for a body and two glasses for legs.' What is she doing?
quiz.explain: She names the shapes in her model.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the shape words

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to build a tall tower. Should I use balls or boxes?
teach.praise: Flat boxes stack, round balls roll. Gappu's tower is tall!
teach.nudge: What happens if I put a ball on top? Why?

learn.hook: Push a ball and push a book. What happens?
points: Round things can roll, like a ball or a bangle.
Things with flat faces slide when we push them.
A cylinder can roll on its side. It slides on its flat end.
A cube cannot roll. It can only slide.

example.q: Can a tin of biscuits roll and slide?
steps: Lay the tin on its curved side. Push. It rolls.
Stand it on its flat end. Push. It slides.
example.answer: Yes, it can roll and slide.

learn.reallife: Wheels roll on the road. A cupboard slides when we push it.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ball is round all over. It rolls easily.
A book can roll down a slope.
A book has flat faces. It slides.
A tin can roll on its curved side.
The curved side lets it roll.
A dice rolls smoothly like a ball.
A dice has flat faces. It tumbles but does not roll smoothly.
A cylinder can slide on its flat end.
Its flat end sits flat, so it can slide.

quiz.q: Which one rolls?
quiz.explain: A marble is round. Round things roll.

quiz.q: Which one will slide, not roll?
quiz.explain: A box has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Why can a bicycle wheel roll?
quiz.explain: Round things roll. A wheel is round.

quiz.q: Arjun pushes a cube. What does it do?
quiz.explain: A cube has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Which can roll on one side and slide on another?
quiz.explain: A tin rolls on its curved side. It slides on its flat end.
quiz.mistake: Picks something that does only one

quiz.q: Aisha wants a toy that rolls down a slide. Which should she pick?
quiz.explain: A ball is round, so it rolls down.

teach.ask: Gappu: Why does my ball roll away but my book stays?
teach.praise: Now I know! Round things roll. Flat things slide!
teach.nudge: What shape is the ball? What does a flat thing do?

learn.hook: Let us test! Push it and see: does it roll, slide or do both?
points: Write R if a thing rolls. Write S if it slides.
Some things do both. A bottle rolls on its side and slides on its bottom.
Test it: push it on the floor or let it go down a slope.
Tick ✓ what it can do. Cross ✗ what it cannot do.

example.q: Test a bottle cap. Does it roll, slide or both?
steps: Stand it on its round edge and push. It rolls.
Lay it flat and push. It slides.

learn.reallife: On the playground, a ball rolls down the slide. You slide down it!

items.text: A bottle can roll and also ___.
A book on a slope will ___.

quiz.q: Riya writes R or S. What should she write for a football?
quiz.explain: A football rolls. R means rolls.

quiz.q: What should Riya write for a brick?
quiz.explain: A brick has flat faces. It slides, so S.

quiz.q: Which can roll and slide both?
quiz.explain: A bottle rolls on its curved side and slides on its flat bottom.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that one thing can do both

quiz.q: Kabir pushes an eraser on the floor. What does it do?
quiz.explain: An eraser has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Joseph tests: ball rolls ✓, book ✗, glass rolls ✓, box ✗. How many things can roll?
quiz.explain: Ball and glass got a tick. That is 2.

quiz.q: A tin can rolls on its side. Can it also slide?
quiz.explain: Stand it on its flat end and push. It slides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a round thing can never slide

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know if a bottle rolls, slides or does both?
teach.praise: Push and test! A bottle does both. Wow!
teach.nudge: What happens on its curved side? And on its flat bottom?

learn.hook: One juicy mango, and friends keep coming! How many are eating now?
points: At the start, 1 parrot eats the mango.
Then 1 more friend comes. Now there are 2.
Each time one more joins, we say the next number.
1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. At the end, 9 friends share the mango!

example.q: 4 animals are eating a mango. 1 more squirrel joins. How many are eating now?
steps: One more joins: say the next number after 4.

learn.reallife: When friends join your game one by one, you count on: 3, 4, 5...

games.title: True or false?
items: When one more joins, the number grows by 1.
If 1 parrot is eating, 1 is eating.

quiz.q: A parrot is eating a mango all alone. How many are eating?
quiz.explain: Just one parrot is eating. That is 1.

quiz.q: 3 squirrels are eating. 1 more joins. How many now?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 3 is 4.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the one who joined

quiz.q: What is 1 more than 6?
quiz.explain: After 6 comes 7.
quiz.mistake: Says the number before instead of after

quiz.q: 7 birds share a mango. 1 more comes. Then 1 more comes. How many now?
quiz.explain: 7, then 8, then 9.
quiz.mistake: Adds only one of the new birds

quiz.q: Friends join one by one. Count on: 5, 6, 7, ___, 9.
quiz.explain: After 7 comes 8, then 9.
quiz.mistake: Skips a number while counting on

quiz.q: Count the mango eaters: 🐦🐦🐦🐦🐦🐦🐦🐦🐦. How many in all?
quiz.explain: Touch each bird once: 1 to 9.

teach.ask: Gappu: 5 friends are eating mango. One more comes. How do I find how many now?
teach.praise: Next number after 5 is 6. Six friends, one mango!
teach.nudge: What number comes right after 5?

learn.hook: Your fingers can show any number up to 10! Let us try.
points: Show 3 birds with 3 fingers: one finger for each bird.
Show the same number with dots: ● ● ●.
Small numbers of dots can be seen at a glance, without counting one by one.
Fingers, dots and birds match when the number is the same.

example.q: 4 sparrows sit on a wire. Show it with fingers and with dots.
steps: Hold up 1 finger for each sparrow: 4 fingers.

learn.reallife: We hold up fingers to tell our age: 6 fingers for 6 years!

quiz.q: 🐦🐦🐦 How many fingers will you show for these birds?
quiz.explain: One finger for each bird. 3 birds, 3 fingers.

quiz.q: Riya shows 5 fingers. How many dots should she draw?
quiz.explain: One dot for each finger. 5 fingers, 5 dots.
quiz.mistake: Draws one dot too many or too few

quiz.q: Kabir draws ● ● ● ● ● ● ●. How many fingers match?
quiz.explain: Count the dots: 1 to 7. Show 7 fingers.

quiz.q: Which dot card matches 2 fingers?
quiz.explain: 2 fingers need 2 dots.
quiz.mistake: Does not match one dot to one finger

quiz.q: Joseph holds up a whole hand and 1 more finger. How many dots match?
quiz.explain: A whole hand is 5. One more is 6.

quiz.q: Which dot card shows the same number as 4 birds?
quiz.explain: 4 birds need 4 dots, one for each.
quiz.mistake: Picks a card with one more or one less

teach.ask: Gappu: I see 3 butterflies. How do I show this with fingers and dots?
teach.praise: 3 fingers, 3 dots, 3 butterflies. All match!
teach.nudge: How many fingers for each butterfly?

learn.hook: It is drawing day! Does every child get a crayon box?
points: Give each child one thing. Draw a line from each child to one thing.
If things are left over, there are more things than children.
If some children get nothing, there are fewer things.
If all match with none left, the numbers are equal.

example.q: 4 children and 3 drawing sheets. Give one sheet to each child. Are there enough?
steps: Match each sheet to a child: 3 children get one.

learn.reallife: At a birthday party, we check there is one plate for each guest.

games.title: True or false?
items: If each child gets one and none is left, the numbers are equal.
4 cups and 6 spoons: there are fewer cups.
3 children and 5 balls: some children get no ball.
There are more balls. Every child gets one and 2 are left.
Drawing lines one to one helps us compare.
The side with extras has more.

quiz.q: 5 children and 5 brushes. One brush each. How many brushes are left?
quiz.explain: Each child got one. No brush is left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks something is always left over

quiz.q: 4 children and 6 crayons. One crayon each. What is true?
quiz.explain: After each child gets one, 2 crayons are left. So more crayons.
quiz.mistake: Does not match one to one

quiz.q: ☕☕☕ 🥄🥄🥄🥄🥄. Which group has fewer?
quiz.explain: 3 cups, 5 spoons. 3 is fewer than 5.

quiz.q: 6 children and 4 sheets. How many children do not get a sheet?
quiz.explain: 4 children get sheets. 2 children are left without.

quiz.q: ☕☕☕☕ 🥄🥄. Circle the group with fewer items.
quiz.explain: 2 spoons and 4 cups. Spoons are fewer.

quiz.q: 3 children each get one pencil. 2 pencils are left. How many pencils were there?
quiz.explain: 3 given out and 2 left. 3 + 2 = 5.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 5 friends and 4 cookies. Does every friend get one?
teach.praise: One each... one friend gets none. 4 is less than 5. Smart!
teach.nudge: If I give one cookie to each friend, is anyone left out?

learn.hook: Riya has 5 mangoes. Arjun has 3. Who has more?
points: More means a bigger number of things.
Less (or fewer) means a smaller number.
Match them one to one. The side with extras has more.
When both match fully, they are the same (equal).

example.q: Riya has 5 mangoes. Arjun has 3. Who has more? How many more?
steps: Match one of Riya's with one of Arjun's.

learn.reallife: At a party, we check who got more sweets! We pick the shorter queue at a shop.

games.title: True or false?
items: 9 is more. It comes later when we count.

quiz.q: Which is more?
quiz.explain: 9 comes after 6 when we count. So 9 is more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the first number is bigger

quiz.q: Which is the least?
quiz.explain: 2 comes first when we count. It is the smallest.

quiz.q: Aisha has 🍬🍬🍬🍬. Joseph has 🍬🍬. Who has fewer sweets?
quiz.explain: Joseph has 2. Aisha has 4. 2 is less than 4.

quiz.q: Kabir has 5 kites. Harpreet has 3 kites. How many more does Kabir have?
quiz.explain: Match 3 kites each. Kabir has 2 extra.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of comparing

quiz.q: Which is one more than 6?
quiz.explain: One more than 6 is the next number: 7.

quiz.q: Meena has 4 bangles. Riya has 4 bangles. What is true?
quiz.explain: Both have 4. So they have the same number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one must always have more

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 worms. My friend has 5. Who has more? How do you know?
teach.praise: Yes! Match them up. Extras mean more!
teach.nudge: Which word do we use for a bigger number? How can I check?

learn.hook: Nani brought a basket of mangoes! Let us count them.
points: Each number is one more than the number before it.
The last number we say tells how many.
We can write numbers as digits: 1, 2, 3.

example.q: What number comes just after 6?

learn.reallife: We count steps on stairs, buttons on a shirt, and candles on a cake.

games.title: Count up
games.prompt: Put the numbers in counting order

quiz.q: What comes just after 4?
quiz.explain: Count 1, 2, 3, 4. Next is 5.
quiz.mistake: Says the number before instead of after

quiz.q: What comes just before 9?
quiz.explain: Count 7, 8, 9. Just before 9 is 8.
quiz.mistake: Says the number after instead of before

quiz.q: Which number is between 6 and 8?
quiz.explain: 6, 7, 8. The number in between is 7.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two

quiz.q: How do we write 'three' as a number?
quiz.explain: Three is written as 3.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the shapes of 3 and 8

quiz.q: Count: 2, 3, 4, ___, 6. What is missing?
quiz.explain: After 4 comes 5. Then 6.

quiz.q: There are 9 steps. Riya has climbed 8. How many more steps to the top?
quiz.explain: From 8, one more step makes 9.
quiz.mistake: Counts the step she is on again

teach.ask: Gappu: I can say 1, 2, 3. What comes next? Why?
teach.praise: Hooray! Each number is one more than before!
teach.nudge: What do we get when we add one more?

learn.hook: Let us write numbers, colour stars and draw fruits!
points: We write numbers with digits: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.
Start a digit at the top and go down.
To colour 5 flowers: colour and count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Then stop.
To draw 4 fruits: draw one and count, until you say 4.

example.q: There are 8 stars. Colour 6 of them. How many stay white?
steps: Count the white ones: 7, 8. That is 2.

learn.reallife: We write numbers on house gates, bus numbers and cake candles.

items.text: To colour 5 flowers, I stop when I say ___.

games.title: True or false?
items: To colour 6 balls, we colour until we say 6.
Count each one as you draw it.
Then you will not draw too many.

quiz.q: How do we write the number 'six'?
quiz.explain: Six is written as 6.

quiz.q: Riya must colour 5 of these flowers: 🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸🌸. How many stay uncoloured?
quiz.explain: 7 flowers, 5 coloured. 6, 7 are left: 2.

quiz.q: Kabir drew 🍌🍌🍌. He must draw 4 fruits. How many more should he draw?
quiz.explain: He has 3. One more makes 4.
quiz.mistake: Draws 4 more instead of finishing at 4

quiz.q: Aisha has to colour 8 stars. Which shows 8?
quiz.explain: Count each row. Only the first one has 8.

quiz.q: Joseph has to colour 6 balls. He has coloured 4. How many more?
quiz.explain: 4, then 5, 6. That is 2 more.

quiz.q: Meena writes how many fingers are on one hand. What does she write?
quiz.explain: One hand has 5 fingers.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have to colour 5 flowers. How do I know when to stop?
teach.praise: Count as you colour and stop at 5. Neat work!
teach.nudge: What number do I say on the last flower?

learn.hook: Kabir has a plate of laddoos. How many can he share?
points: Touch each thing once and say a number.
Do not skip any. Do not count any twice.
The last number you say is how many in all.
Zero (0) means none at all.

example.q: Count: 🪔 🪔 🪔 🪔 🪔 🪔. How many diyas?

learn.reallife: We count rotis at dinner, kids in a team and diyas at Diwali.

quiz.q: How many mangoes? 🥭🥭🥭🥭🥭
quiz.explain: Touch and count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

quiz.q: How many diyas? 🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔
quiz.explain: Count each diya once: 1 to 7.

quiz.q: Arjun has no balloons. How many balloons does he have?
quiz.explain: No balloons means zero. We write 0.

quiz.q: How many stars? ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Meena counts 1, 2, 3, 4 laddoos. How many laddoos are there?
quiz.explain: The last number she said is 4. So there are 4.
quiz.mistake: Gives the first number said, not the last

quiz.q: How many footballs? 🏏 ⚽ ⚽ ⚽
quiz.explain: 🏏 is a bat, not a ball. Count only the footballs: 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts the bat as a ball too

teach.ask: Gappu: I counted my grapes and got a new answer each time! Help!
teach.praise: Touch each one once. The last number is the answer. Got it!
teach.nudge: How many times should I count each grape? Which number is the answer?

learn.hook: Dot-to-dot! Join 1 to 9 and see what picture appears.
points: In dot-to-dot, start at 1. Go to 2, then 3, all the way to 9.
If we skip a dot, the picture goes wrong.
To arrange cards, find the smallest first. Then the next one.
Smallest to largest: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

example.q: Cards: 7, 2, 5. Put them from smallest to largest.

learn.reallife: Page numbers in a book and seat numbers in a bus go in order.

games.title: True or false?
items: In dot-to-dot, we go from 1 to 2 to 3.
9 is the last dot in a 1 to 9 picture.

quiz.q: In a dot-to-dot, you are at dot 4. Which dot is next?
quiz.explain: After 4 comes 5.
quiz.mistake: Goes backwards or skips a dot

quiz.q: Cards 6, 1, 3. Which is the smallest?
quiz.explain: 1 comes first when we count.

quiz.q: Put 8, 4, 6 from smallest to largest. Which card is in the middle?
quiz.explain: In order: 4, 6, 8. 6 is in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the cards in the given order

quiz.q: Which is in order from smallest to largest?
quiz.explain: 2 is less than 5, and 5 is less than 9.

quiz.q: Riya joins dots 1, 2, 3, 5. Which dot did she miss?
quiz.explain: After 3 comes 4, then 5.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice a gap in the order

quiz.q: Cards 9, 7, 8. Smallest to largest, which card goes last?
quiz.explain: In order: 7, 8, 9. 9 is last.
quiz.mistake: Picks the smallest for the last place

teach.ask: Gappu: My cards are 5, 3, 8. How do I put them in order?
teach.praise: 3, 5, 8! Smallest first. Hooray!
teach.nudge: Which card is the smallest? Start with that one.

learn.hook: 5 mangoes and 3 mangoes. Together, how many? Let us join groups!
points: Two small groups can join to make a number.
🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎 and 🍎🍎🍎 make 8.
7 can be 3 and 4, or 5 and 2, or 6 and 1.
Split a number into two parts. Join the parts to get it back.

example.q: Which two groups make 7: 4 umbrellas, 3 umbrellas or 5 umbrellas?

learn.reallife: Laddoos in two boxes, or shoes on two racks, can be joined to find how many in all.

quiz.q: 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎 and 🍎🍎🍎. How many fruits in all?
quiz.explain: 5 and 3 make 8.

quiz.q: Which two groups make 7 umbrellas?
quiz.explain: 4 and 3 make 7. The others make 8.
quiz.mistake: Does not count both groups together

quiz.q: Riya splits 6 beads into two parts. One part has 2. How many in the other?
quiz.explain: 2 and 4 make 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the other part

quiz.q: Which is NOT a way to make 5?
quiz.explain: 3 and 3 make 6, not 5.

quiz.q: 9 is 5 and ___.
quiz.explain: 5 and 4 make 9.

quiz.q: Kabir has 8 marbles in two pockets. One pocket has all 8. How many in the other?
quiz.explain: 8 and 0 make 8. The other pocket is empty.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a part can be zero

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 6 seeds. Can I put them in two heaps in different ways?
teach.praise: 3 and 3, 2 and 4, 1 and 5. So many ways to make 6!
teach.nudge: If one heap has 2 seeds, how many are in the other?

learn.hook: Dotty Bug has spots on her back. How many? Let us count!
points: Count the dots on a bug to know its number.
We can make dot designs with seeds, pebbles, buttons or bindis.
Dots in a neat pattern, like 2 on top and 2 below, are quick to read.
The same number can look different: ●●●● in a line and ●● over ●● are both 4.

example.q: Bug A has ● ● ● in a line. Bug B has ● on top and ● ● below. Who has more dots?

learn.reallife: Rangoli dots, bindis on a card and seeds in a flower design all show numbers.

quiz.q: Dotty Bug has ●●●●●● on her back. How many dots?
quiz.explain: Count each dot once: 1 to 6.

quiz.q: Riya makes a design with 3 bindis on top and 2 below. How many bindis?
quiz.explain: 3 and 2 make 5.

quiz.q: Which shows the same number as ●●●●?
quiz.explain: 2 and 2 make 4. It just looks different.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a new shape means a new number

quiz.q: Kabir uses 7 seeds for a flower design. He adds 1 seed in the middle. How many seeds now?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 7 is 8.

quiz.q: Bug A: ● ● ●. Bug B: ●● and ●. What is true?
quiz.explain: Bug A has 3. Bug B has 2 and 1, which is 3.
quiz.mistake: Judges by how the dots look, not how many

quiz.q: Aisha makes 2 rows of buttons with 4 in each row. How many buttons?
quiz.explain: 4 and 4 make 8.

teach.ask: Gappu: One bug has dots in a line. One has dots in a square. How do I know who has more?
teach.praise: Count both! Same count means same number, even if it looks different.
teach.nudge: Did I count the dots, or just look at the shape?

learn.hook: Roll the dice! Colour the boxes! Who will win?
points: A dice has 6 faces with dots from 1 to 6.
⚀ is 1, ⚁ is 2, ⚂ is 3, ⚃ is 4, ⚄ is 5, ⚅ is 6.
Roll the dice and colour that many boxes.
The player with more coloured boxes wins.

example.q: Riya rolls ⚃. Kabir rolls ⚁. Each colours that many boxes. Who has more?

learn.reallife: We use a dice in Ludo and in Snakes and Ladders.

quiz.q: Arjun rolls ⚄. How many boxes does he colour?
quiz.explain: ⚄ has 5 dots. He colours 5 boxes.

quiz.q: Which dice face shows 3?
quiz.explain: ⚂ has 3 dots.

quiz.q: Meena rolls ⚅. Joseph rolls ⚃. Who colours more boxes?
quiz.explain: ⚅ is 6 and ⚃ is 4. 6 is more.

quiz.q: What is the most dots on one face of a dice?
quiz.explain: The faces go from 1 to 6. The most is 6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a dice goes up to 10

quiz.q: Aisha rolls ⚁ and then ⚂. How many boxes does she colour in all?
quiz.explain: 2 and 3 make 5.

quiz.q: Kabir coloured 4 boxes. Riya coloured 4 boxes. Who wins?
quiz.explain: Both have 4. Equal means a tie.

teach.ask: Gappu: I rolled ⚄. What do I do now?
teach.praise: 5 dots, so colour 5 boxes. Go, Gappu!
teach.nudge: How many dots are on the dice? What do I colour?

learn.hook: All the birds flew away! How many are on the branch now?
points: Birds fly away from a branch one by one.
When all fly away, none are left.
None is zero. We write it as 0.
At night we see 0 suns. An empty box has 0 sweets.
0 comes just before 1.

example.q: 3 birds sit on a branch. One flies away, then another, then the last. How many are left?

learn.reallife: An empty water bottle has 0 water. A cricket team with no runs has a score of 0.

games.title: True or false?
items: The sun is not in the night sky.

quiz.q: 4 birds sit on a branch. All 4 fly away. How many are left?
quiz.explain: All flew away, so none are left. That is 0.

quiz.q: How many suns can you see in the sky at night?
quiz.explain: The sun is not in the sky at night. So 0.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that none is a number

quiz.q: Riya's lunch box is empty. How many idlis are in it?
quiz.explain: Empty means no idlis. That is 0.

quiz.q: Which number comes just before 1?
quiz.explain: Counting back from 1 gives 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks counting starts at 1 with nothing before

quiz.q: 3 birds on a branch. 1 flies away. How many are left?
quiz.explain: 3 take away 1 is 2.

quiz.q: Which is the least: 3, 0 or 1?
quiz.explain: 0 means none. It is less than any other count.

teach.ask: Gappu: All my eggs hatched and the chicks walked away. How many chicks are in my nest?
teach.praise: Zero chicks! 0 means none. Peep peep!
teach.nudge: If none are left, what number do we say?

topics.title: Tenth birthday: strings and frames of 10

learn.hook: Joseph turns 10 today! Let us count candles, diyas and beads.
points: Joseph's cake has 10 candles. The room has 10 diyas.
A bead string of 10: count the beads, then add more to reach 10.
A ten frame has 2 rows of 5 boxes. That is 10 boxes.
When every box has a button, the frame shows 10.

example.q: A string has 6 beads. Draw more to make 10. How many more?

learn.reallife: Many pencil packs hold 10 pencils. Some sweet boxes hold 10 laddoos, 2 rows of 5.

items.text: A ten frame has 2 rows of ___ boxes.
A string has 8 beads. ___ more make 10.
Joseph has 9 candles. He needs ___ more for 10.

games.title: True or false?
items: A full ten frame has 10 buttons.
One button in each of 10 boxes.
A ten frame has 3 rows of 5.
A string with 7 beads needs 3 more to make 10.
If one box is empty, the frame shows 10.

quiz.q: Joseph's cake has 10 candles. 7 are lit. How many are not lit?
quiz.explain: 7 and 3 make 10. So 3 are not lit.
quiz.mistake: Counts one too many or too few

quiz.q: A ten frame has 2 rows of 5 boxes. How many boxes in all?
quiz.explain: 5 and 5 make 10.

quiz.q: A ten frame has 8 buttons. How many boxes are empty?
quiz.explain: 8 and 2 make 10.

quiz.q: Riya's bead string has 5 beads. She wants 10. How many more?
quiz.explain: 5 and 5 make 10.

quiz.q: A ten frame has just 1 empty box. What number does it show?
quiz.explain: 10 boxes with 1 empty means 9 buttons.

quiz.q: Count the diyas at the party: 🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔. How many?
quiz.explain: Count each diya once: 1 to 10.

teach.ask: Gappu: My ten frame has 7 seeds. How many more seeds fill it?
teach.praise: 3 empty boxes, so 3 more seeds make 10. Full frame!
teach.nudge: How many boxes does a full frame have?

learn.hook: Ten fingers, ten toes! Ten is a special number.
points: 10 comes just after 9.
Two numbers can join to make 10, like 6 and 4.
Your two hands have 10 fingers in all.
10 things make one group of ten.

example.q: Arjun has 7 marbles. How many more does he need to make 10?

learn.reallife: Ten fingers help us count. A packet of 10 pencils is one ten.

quiz.q: How many fingers on two hands?
quiz.explain: 5 on one hand and 5 on the other. 5 and 5 make 10.

quiz.q: 8 laddoos are on a plate. How many more make 10?
quiz.explain: Count on from 8: 9, 10. That is 2 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 and 10, or counts one extra

quiz.q: What comes just after 9?
quiz.explain: After 9 comes 10.

quiz.q: 4 and ___ make 10.
quiz.explain: Count on from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 6.

quiz.q: Riya has 5 red bangles and 5 green bangles. How many in all?
quiz.explain: 5 and 5 make 10.
quiz.mistake: Writes the numbers side by side

quiz.q: A box holds 10 pencils. It has 3. How many more fit?
quiz.explain: Count on from 3 to 10: that is 7 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding what is missing

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 6 seeds. How do I find how many more make 10?
teach.praise: Count on from 6 to 10. Four more! Yay!
teach.nudge: What number do I stop at? How do I count up?

learn.hook: Put a stick in a row of 10 beads. What two numbers do you get?
points: Put 10 beads in a row. A stick between them splits them into two parts.
Stick after 3 beads: 3 and 7. Stick after 6 beads: 6 and 4.
Partner finger game: you show some fingers, your friend shows the rest to make 10.
Every split still makes 10 in all.

example.q: 10 marbles are split by a stick. The left side has 2. How many are on the right?

learn.reallife: Sharing 10 toffees between two friends can be done in many ways.

games.title: Splits of 10
games.prompt: Left part from smallest to largest

quiz.q: Partner game: Meena shows 4 fingers. How many must Arjun show to make 10?
quiz.explain: 4 and 6 make 10.

quiz.q: 10 beads in a row. A stick goes after the 3rd bead. How many beads are after the stick?
quiz.explain: 3 and 7 make 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts the beads before the stick

quiz.q: Which pair splits 10?
quiz.explain: 6 and 4 make 10. The others make 9.

quiz.q: Riya splits 10 shells. The left part has 5. How many in the right part?
quiz.explain: 5 and 5 make 10.

quiz.q: Joseph shows 8 fingers. His friend shows 2. How many fingers in all?
quiz.explain: 8 and 2 make 10.

quiz.q: 10 beads. The stick is after the 9th bead. How many beads are after it?
quiz.explain: 9 and 1 make 10.

teach.ask: Gappu: I put a stick after 6 of my 10 beads. How many are on the other side?
teach.praise: 6 and 4 make 10. Clever split!
teach.nudge: How many beads in all? How many on one side?

learn.hook: Bundle 10 sticks with a rubber band. That is one ten!
points: 10 ones make 1 ten.
13 is 1 ten and 3 ones.
In 16, the 1 shows the ten. The 6 shows the ones.
20 is 2 tens and 0 ones.

example.q: Harpreet has 1 bundle of 10 sticks and 4 loose sticks. How many sticks?

learn.reallife: Bundles of 10 sticks are quick to count. Pencils come in packs of 10. It makes counting fast.

games.title: True or false?
items: A bundle of 10 ones is one ten.

quiz.q: 1 ten and 6 ones make ___.
quiz.explain: 1 ten is 10. 10 and 6 make 16.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 and 6, or writes the digits backwards

quiz.q: How many ones are in 13?
quiz.explain: 13 is 1 ten and 3 ones.

quiz.q: How many tens are in 20?
quiz.explain: 10 and 10 make 20. That is 2 tens.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 0 or gives the whole number

quiz.q: Kabir has 10 laddoos in a box and 5 loose. How many laddoos?
quiz.explain: 10 and 5 make 15.

quiz.q: Which number has 1 ten and 9 ones?
quiz.explain: 1 ten is 10. 10 and 9 make 19.

quiz.q: Meena has 17 beads. She makes a group of 10. How many beads are left over?
quiz.explain: 17 is 1 ten and 7 ones. 7 beads are left over.
quiz.mistake: Gives the tens digit instead of ones

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 15 sticks. How can I show them quickly?
teach.praise: Make a bundle of 10. Keep 5 loose. That is 15!
teach.nudge: Can I make a bundle of ten? What about the extra ones?

learn.hook: So many sweets! Circle ten first, then counting is easy.
points: To count many things, first circle a group of ten.
Then count on the rest: 11, 12, 13...
A full ten frame is 10. A second frame shows the extra ones.
1 full frame and 4 more dots show 14.

example.q: There are 16 sweets. Circle 10. How many are outside the circle? What is the number?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers count coins and bananas in tens to count faster.

quiz.q: Count the flowers: 🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼🌼
quiz.explain: Circle 10, then count on 11, 12, 13.
quiz.mistake: Loses count in a big group

quiz.q: One full ten frame and 5 more dots. What number is it?
quiz.explain: 10 and 5 make 15.

quiz.q: Aisha has 18 bangles. She circles 10. How many are outside the circle?
quiz.explain: 10 and 8 make 18.

quiz.q: To show 12, Kabir fills one ten frame. How many dots go in the second frame?
quiz.explain: 10 and 2 make 12.
quiz.mistake: Puts all 12 in the second frame

quiz.explain: Two groups of ten make 20.

quiz.q: Which shows 17?
quiz.explain: 10 and 7 make 17.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tens and the ones

teach.ask: Gappu: There are 14 seeds. How do I count them fast?
teach.praise: Circle 10, then 11, 12, 13, 14! Fast counting!
teach.nudge: What group should I make first?

learn.hook: After 10, the numbers keep going! Let us count to 20.
points: Each number is one more than the one before.
20 is two groups of ten.

example.q: What number comes between 14 and 16?

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, page numbers and house numbers use these numbers.

quiz.q: What comes just after 17?
quiz.explain: 17, then 18.

quiz.q: What comes just before 20?
quiz.explain: 18, 19, 20. Just before 20 is 19.

quiz.q: Which number is between 12 and 14?
quiz.explain: 12, 13, 14. 13 is in between.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two

quiz.q: Which is bigger, 18 or 15?
quiz.explain: 18 comes after 15 when counting. So 18 is bigger.

quiz.q: Count: 15, 16, ___, 18. What is missing?
quiz.explain: After 16 comes 17.

quiz.q: How do we write 'twelve'?
quiz.explain: Twelve is 1 ten and 2 ones. We write 12.

teach.ask: Gappu: I can count to 10. What comes after that?
teach.praise: Wow! 11, 12 ... all the way to 20!
teach.nudge: What comes after 10? Does each number go up by one?

topics.title: Biggest, smallest and in order to 20

learn.hook: Who has the tallest tower? Let us compare numbers up to 20!
points: The smallest number comes first when we count. The biggest comes last.
Biggest to smallest: 18, 15, 11, 6.
With same-size blocks, the tower with the most blocks is the tallest.
Dot-to-dot to 20: join 1, 2, 3, all the way to 20, in order.

example.q: Find the biggest and the smallest: 14, 9, 17, 12.
steps: Count up: 9 comes first, so 9 is the smallest.
17 comes last, so 17 is the biggest.

learn.reallife: In a race, the child with the biggest score wins a prize.

games.title: True or false?
items: A tower of 12 blocks is taller than a tower of 8 same blocks.
More same blocks make it taller.
The tower with the fewest blocks is the shortest.
When all the blocks are the same size.

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 15, 7, 11?
quiz.explain: 7 comes first when we count.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the last digit only

quiz.q: Which is the biggest: 18, 20, 9?
quiz.explain: 20 comes last when we count.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 9 is big because 9 is a big digit

quiz.q: Put 12, 19, 5 from biggest to smallest. Which comes first?
quiz.explain: 19 is the biggest, so it comes first.

quiz.q: Tower A has 9 blocks, Tower B has 14, Tower C has 11. Which has the most blocks?
quiz.explain: 14 is more than 11 and 9.

quiz.q: Which tower has the fewest blocks: A has 13, B has 16, C has 10?
quiz.explain: 10 is less than 13 and 16.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tower with the most

quiz.q: Dot-to-dot: you are at dot 17. Which dot is next?
quiz.explain: After 17 comes 18.

teach.ask: Gappu: My towers have 8, 15 and 11 blocks. Which is the tallest and which is the shortest?
teach.praise: 15 is tallest, 8 is shortest. Super sorting!
teach.nudge: Which number comes last when we count? Which comes first?

learn.hook: Two friends bring sweets to share. How many sweets now?
points: Adding means putting things together.
We use the plus sign + to add.
The equal sign = shows the answer.
Start with the bigger number. Count on the smaller one.

example.q: Riya has 4 laddoos. Mummy gives her 3 more. How many now?

learn.reallife: We add when friends join a game or more sweets come to the plate.

quiz.q: 🍎🍎🍎 and 🍎🍎. How many apples in all?
quiz.explain: 3 and 2 make 5. Count all: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts one group only, or one extra

quiz.q: What is 4 + 4?
quiz.explain: Start at 4. Count on 4: 5, 6, 7, 8.
quiz.mistake: Writes the two numbers side by side

quiz.q: Arjun has 5 marbles. He finds 2 more. How many now?
quiz.explain: Start at 5. Count on 2: 6, 7.

quiz.q: 6 children play cricket. 3 more join. How many play now?
quiz.explain: Start at 6. Count on 3: 7, 8, 9.

quiz.q: What is 7 + 0?
quiz.explain: Adding 0 adds nothing. So it stays 7.

quiz.q: Meena has 2 red balloons and 6 blue ones. How many balloons?
quiz.explain: Start at 6. Count on 2: 7, 8.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 berries. I find 2 more. How do I know how many I have?
teach.praise: Put them together and count on. 5 berries! Yum!
teach.nudge: Do I add or take away? How do I count them?

topics.title: Add and draw: family, fingers and toes

learn.hook: How many fingers and toes do you have? More than you think!
points: To show 3 + 2, draw 3 balls. Then draw 2 more. Count them all.
Count your family and a friend's family to find how many in all.
We have 10 fingers on our hands and 10 toes on our feet.
10 fingers and 10 toes make 20 in all.

example.q: Riya's family has 4 people. Aisha's family has 5. How many people in all?

learn.reallife: When two families meet for a festival, we add to know how many plates to lay out.

items.text: I drew 🎈🎈🎈, then 2 more. Now there are ___.
3 fingers up on one hand and 4 on the other show ___.

games.title: True or false?
items: To show 2 + 4, draw 2, then draw 4 more.
A family of 3 and a family of 3 make 9.

quiz.q: Kabir draws 4 stars. Then he draws 3 more. How many stars now?
quiz.explain: 4 and 3 more make 7.

quiz.q: Meena's family has 3 people. Joseph's family has 6. How many people in all?
quiz.explain: Start at 6 and count on 3: 7, 8, 9.

quiz.q: How many fingers and toes do you have in all?
quiz.explain: 10 fingers and 10 toes make 20.

quiz.q: Aisha shows 5 fingers on one hand and 2 on the other. How many fingers?
quiz.explain: 5 and 2 make 7.

quiz.q: How many toes are on your two feet?
quiz.explain: 5 toes on each foot. 5 and 5 make 10.

quiz.q: Harpreet shows all the fingers of one hand and 4 of the other. How many fingers?
quiz.explain: A whole hand is 5. 5 and 4 make 9.

teach.ask: Gappu: Birds have no fingers! How many fingers and toes do you have altogether?
teach.praise: 10 fingers and 10 toes make 20. Wow!
teach.nudge: How many fingers? How many toes? Now join them.

learn.hook: Roll, win and tick! Who will win the most rounds?
points: Two players roll a dice. The bigger number wins that round.
Put a tick ✓ on the scoreboard for each win.
At the end, count the ticks for each player.
The player with more ticks won more rounds.

example.q: Riya has ✓✓✓✓. Kabir has ✓✓. Who won more rounds? By how many?

learn.reallife: In cricket, the scoreboard shows runs. More runs means the team is ahead.

quiz.q: Meena's scoreboard shows ✓✓✓✓✓. How many rounds did she win?
quiz.explain: Count the ticks: 1 to 5.

quiz.q: Arjun has ✓✓✓. Joseph has ✓✓✓✓✓✓. Who won more rounds?
quiz.explain: Joseph has 6 ticks. Arjun has 3. 6 is more.

quiz.q: Riya has ✓✓✓✓. Aisha has ✓✓. How many more rounds did Riya win?
quiz.explain: 4 is 2 more than 2.
quiz.mistake: Adds the ticks instead of comparing

quiz.q: Kabir rolls ⚄. Harpreet rolls ⚂. Who gets a tick?
quiz.explain: ⚄ is 5. ⚂ is 3. 5 is bigger, so Kabir wins the round.

quiz.q: They played 7 rounds with no ties. Riya won 4. Kabir won the rest. How many did Kabir win?
quiz.explain: 4 and 3 make 7.
quiz.mistake: Gives Kabir the same as Riya

quiz.q: What does one tick on the scoreboard show?
quiz.explain: We put one tick each time a player wins a round.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what the tick stands for

teach.ask: Gappu: I have ✓✓✓ and my friend has ✓✓✓✓✓. Who won more?
teach.praise: 5 ticks beat 3 ticks. Your friend won more. Good game!
teach.nudge: How many ticks does each of us have?

learn.hook: Hop, hop, hop on the number strip! Where will you land?
points: Colour 3 beads red and 4 beads blue. Count all the beads: 7.
On a number strip, start at the first number.
Hop forward as many steps as the second number.
The number where you land is the sum.

example.q: Hop to find 5 + 3.

learn.reallife: Hopscotch on the school ground is like hopping on a number strip.

quiz.q: Riya colours 3 beads red and 4 beads blue. How many beads in all?
quiz.explain: 3 and 4 make 7.

quiz.q: Start at 6 on the number strip. Hop 2 forward. Where do you land?
quiz.explain: 6, then 7, then 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts the start as a hop

quiz.q: How do you find 4 + 5 on a number strip?
quiz.explain: Start at the first number and hop the second number.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where to start

quiz.q: Kabir hops 3 and lands on 9. Where did he start?
quiz.explain: 6 + 3 = 9. He started at 6.

quiz.q: Hop to find 2 + 7. Where do you land?
quiz.explain: Start at 2 and hop 7: you land on 9.

quiz.q: A mala has 5 green beads and 5 yellow beads. How many beads?
quiz.explain: 5 and 5 make 10.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find 3 + 4 on the number strip?
teach.praise: Start at 3, hop 4, land on 7. Hop hop hooray!
teach.nudge: Where do I start? How many hops?

learn.hook: Kabir and Meena add in different ways. Can both be right?
points: Kabir counts all: 1, 2, 3, and so on. Meena counts on from the bigger number. Both get the same sum.
3 + 4 and 4 + 3 are both 7. The order does not change the sum.
A number can be made from two parts: 6 is 2 + 4, 3 + 3 or 5 + 1.
Match each sum with its answer, then check.

example.q: Find 2 + 6 in two ways.
steps: Way 2: start at 6 and count on 2: 7, 8.

learn.reallife: Some friends add on fingers, some on beads. The answer stays the same!

quiz.q: Riya knows 5 + 2 = 7. What is 2 + 5?
quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the sum.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a new order gives a new sum

quiz.q: Joseph counts all to find 3 + 5. Aisha counts on from 5. Who is right?
quiz.explain: Both ways give 8. Any correct way is fine.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is only one right way

quiz.q: Which pair makes 9?
quiz.mistake: Does not add the parts to check
Writes the whole instead of the part

quiz.q: Which is the same as 4 + 3?
quiz.explain: 3 + 4 uses the same numbers, so it is also 7.
quiz.mistake: Changes the numbers, not just the order

quiz.q: Kabir has 8 marbles in two bags. One bag has 6. How many in the other?
quiz.explain: 6 and 2 make 8.

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend says 2 + 7 = 9 and I say 7 + 2 = 9. Who is right?
teach.praise: Both right! Changing the order keeps the sum the same.
teach.nudge: Do 2 + 7 and 7 + 2 use the same numbers?

learn.hook: Is it a plus story or a minus story? Let us find out!
points: More coming? Then add with +.
Some going away? Then take away with -.
Adding makes the number bigger (but adding 0 keeps it the same).
Taking away makes the number smaller (but taking away 0 keeps it the same).

example.q: There are 4 cows. 3 more cows come. Add or take away?

learn.reallife: Guests arriving means add. Sweets eaten means take away.

quiz.q: 4 ducks swim. 2 more come. Add or take away?
quiz.explain: More ducks come. So we add.
quiz.mistake: Takes away when more are coming

quiz.q: 4 ducks swim. 2 more come. How many ducks now?
8 crayons are in a box. 3 fall out. How many are in the box?
quiz.explain: Some go away, so take away. 8 - 3 = 5.

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 5 + 2 or 5 - 2?
quiz.mistake: Thinks plus and minus give the same answer

quiz.q: 3 + ___ = 8. What is missing?
quiz.explain: Count on from 3 to 8: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. That is 5.

quiz.q: Riya has 9 diyas. 4 blow out. How many still glow?
quiz.explain: Some go out, so take away. 9 - 4 = 5.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know if a story needs plus or minus?
teach.praise: More coming means add. Going away means take away. Smart!
teach.nudge: What do I do when more come? What about when some go away?

topics.title: Make an addition story; sum puzzle

learn.hook: Open your bag! Can you make a story that adds?
points: An addition story has two groups that join.
'I have 3 books. I put 2 more in my bag. Now I have 5.'
Sum puzzle: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.
To make every line add to 6, put 1, 2 and 3 once in each line.

example.q: A puzzle line has 1 and 2 filled in. Which number goes in the empty box so the line makes 6?

learn.reallife: At home: 'Mummy bought 4 apples and 2 bananas. That is 6 fruits.'

items.text: I have 2 pencils and 3 crayons. I have ___ things.

games.title: True or false?
items: 'I had 4 books. I got 2 more.' is an addition story.
A puzzle line with 2, 2 and 2 uses 1, 2, 3 once.
'3 birds flew away' is an addition story.

quiz.q: Meena's bag has 4 books and 3 notebooks. How many in all?
quiz.explain: 4 and 3 make 7.

quiz.q: Which is an addition story?
options: I had 2 pens. Papa gave me 3 more.
I had 4 pens. I gave 1 away.
quiz.explain: Getting more means the groups join. We add.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up adding and taking away

quiz.q: A line has 2 and 3. Which number makes the line add to 6?
quiz.explain: 2 + 3 = 5. 1 more makes 6.
quiz.mistake: Repeats a number already in the line

quiz.q: What is 1 + 2 + 3?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the numbers

quiz.q: A line has 3 and 1. Which number completes it to make 6?
quiz.explain: 3 + 1 = 4. 2 more makes 6.
quiz.mistake: Repeats a number already in the line

quiz.q: Arjun's bag has 5 pencils and 4 erasers. How many things in his story?
quiz.explain: 5 and 4 make 9.

teach.ask: Gappu: Can you tell me an addition story about things in your bag?
teach.praise: What a story! Two groups joined and you found the total.
teach.nudge: What two groups are in my story? How many in all?

learn.hook: Beep beep! At each stop, a child gets down. Who is left?
points: The school bus has 5 children. At each stop, 1 child gets down.
5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0: one fewer each time.
When nobody is left, there are 0 children.
Draw the things, cross out the ones taken away, count the rest. Write it: 5 - 2 = 3.

example.q: 6 children are on the bus. 1 gets down at each of 2 stops. How many are left?

learn.reallife: On the way home, the bus gets emptier at every stop.

games.title: Bus stops
games.prompt: Children on the bus, from the start to the end

quiz.q: 5 children are on the bus. 1 gets down. How many are left?
quiz.explain: One fewer than 5 is 4.
quiz.mistake: Adds the child instead of taking away

quiz.q: 4 children are on the bus. 1 gets down at each stop. After 4 stops, how many are left?
quiz.explain: 4, 3, 2, 1, 0. Nobody is left.

quiz.q: 3 children. 1 gets down at the first stop and 1 at the next. How many are left?
quiz.explain: 3, then 2, then 1.

quiz.q: Riya draws 6 kites and crosses out 2. How many kites are not crossed out?
quiz.explain: 6 take away 2 is 4.

quiz.q: Which sentence matches 7 balls with 3 crossed out?
quiz.explain: 7 balls, 3 taken away, 4 left.

quiz.q: Only 1 child is on the bus. She gets down. How many are left?
quiz.explain: 1 take away 1 leaves 0. The bus is empty.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bus can't be empty

teach.ask: Gappu: 3 chicks were on my back. One hopped off at each stop. How many are left after 3 stops?
teach.praise: 3, 2, 1, 0. Zero chicks left. My back is free!
teach.nudge: What number do we get when nobody is left?

learn.hook: Five birds sit on a wire. Two fly away. How many stay?
points: Subtracting means taking away.
We use the minus sign - to take away.
Count back to find what is left.
Taking away 0 leaves the same number.

example.q: Kabir has 8 grapes. He eats 3. How many are left?

learn.reallife: When we eat sweets, the plate has fewer. When friends leave, fewer play.

games.title: True or false?
items: Take away all 5. None are left.

quiz.q: 5 birds sit on a wire. 2 fly away. How many stay?
quiz.explain: Count back 2 from 5: 4, 3. 3 birds stay.

quiz.q: What is 9 - 3?
quiz.explain: Count back 3 from 9: 8, 7, 6.

quiz.q: Aisha has 7 balloons. 4 pop. How many are left?
quiz.explain: Count back 4 from 7: 6, 5, 4, 3.

quiz.q: Joseph has 6 rotis. He eats all 6. How many are left?
quiz.explain: All are eaten. None are left. 6 - 6 = 0.

quiz.q: What is 8 - 0?
quiz.explain: Taking away nothing leaves 8.

quiz.q: Harpreet has 9 stickers. She gives 5 to Riya. How many does she keep?
quiz.explain: Count back 5 from 9: 8, 7, 6, 5, 4.

teach.ask: Gappu: I had 6 worms. I ate 2. How many are left? How do you know?
teach.praise: Count back from 6: 5, 4. Four left! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Do I take away or add? How do I count back?

learn.hook: A hand covers some dots! How many are hiding?
points: A card has 7 dots. A hand hides some. We see 4.
Hidden = all the dots take away the dots we see: 7 - 4 = 3.
Check by adding: 4 seen + 3 hidden = 7.
Adding and taking away are linked: 4 + 3 = 7, so 7 - 3 = 4.

example.q: 8 dots in all. 5 can be seen. How many are hidden?

learn.reallife: If you know 10 children are in a group and 7 are in the room, 3 must be outside.

quiz.q: A card has 6 dots. A paper hides some. You see 4. How many are hidden?
quiz.explain: 4 and 2 make 6. So 2 are hidden.

quiz.q: 9 dots in all. 3 can be seen. How many are hidden?
quiz.explain: 3 and 6 make 9.

quiz.q: Aisha has 7 shells. Some are under a cup. 2 are outside. How many are under the cup?
quiz.explain: 2 and 5 make 7.
If 5 and 3 make 8, then taking 3 from 8 leaves 5.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the link between + and -

quiz.q: Kabir sees 4 dots. He knows 4 more are hidden. How many dots in all?
quiz.explain: 4 seen and 4 hidden make 8.

quiz.q: Which fact goes with 2 + 5 = 7?
quiz.explain: The same three numbers: 2, 5 and 7.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fact with a different whole

teach.ask: Gappu: My card has 9 dots. My wing hides some. I see 6. How many are hidden?
teach.praise: 9 - 6 = 3 hidden. And 6 + 3 = 9 checks it!
teach.nudge: How many in all? How many can I see?

learn.hook: Hop backwards on the number strip! Careful, little frog!
points: To find 9 - 3, start at 9 on the number strip.
Hop back 3: 8, 7, 6. Land on 6.
You can also count up from 3 to 9, or use your fingers.
Any way is fine if the answer is right. Check by adding: 6 + 3 = 9.

example.q: Find 8 - 5 by hopping back.

learn.reallife: Counting down for a rocket launch is like hopping back: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1!

games.title: True or false?
items: Hopping back makes the number bigger.
Going back gives a smaller number.

quiz.q: Start at 9. Hop back 3. Where do you land?
Find 8 - 5.
quiz.explain: Hop back 5 from 8: 7, 6, 5, 4, 3.

quiz.q: Meena counts up from 4 to 9 to find 9 - 4. How many hops does she make?
quiz.mistake: Counts the starting number as a hop

quiz.q: Joseph says 7 - 3 = 4. How can he check?
options: Add 4 + 3 and see if it is 7
quiz.explain: 4 + 3 = 7, so his answer is right.
quiz.mistake: Does not know adding checks taking away

quiz.q: Use the number strip. What is 10 - 6?
quiz.explain: Hop back 6 from 10: you land on 4.

quiz.q: Riya hops back 2 from 6. Kabir counts up from 2 to 6. What do they both get?
quiz.explain: Both ways give 6 - 2 = 4.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find 7 - 2 on the number strip?
teach.praise: Start at 7, hop back 2, land on 5. And 5 + 2 = 7 checks it!
teach.nudge: Do I hop forward or back? Where do I start?

learn.hook: The farm has lots of vegetables! Let us add them up.
points: Start with the bigger number. Count on the smaller one.
Make 10 first. Then add what is left.
9 + 4: give 1 to 9 to make 10. Then 10 + 3 = 13.
Changing the order gives the same sum. 3 + 8 = 8 + 3.

example.q: Meena picks 8 carrots and 5 more. How many carrots?

learn.reallife: We add runs in cricket and coins in a piggy bank.

quiz.q: What is 9 + 4?
quiz.explain: Make 10: 9 + 1 = 10. Then add the 3 left: 13.
quiz.mistake: Loses or adds one while counting on

quiz.q: What is 10 + 6?
quiz.explain: 1 ten and 6 ones make 16.

quiz.q: Arjun has 7 tomatoes. He picks 7 more. How many now?
quiz.explain: 7 + 3 = 10. Then 4 more: 14.
quiz.mistake: Counts one too many or too few

quiz.q: Which is the same as 5 + 8?
quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the sum. Both are 13.

quiz.q: What is 6 + 9?
Kabir has 11 peas. He finds 8 more. How many peas?
quiz.explain: Start at 11. Count on 8: up to 19.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I add 8 and 5 quickly?
teach.praise: Make 10 first, then add 3. It is 13!
teach.nudge: Can I make a ten first? How many are left to add?

topics.title: Fill the blank: mala and hops

learn.hook: Slide the beads on a mala and hop on the line to find big sums!
points: Fill the blank to finish a sum: 7 + 5 = ___ asks what 7 and 5 make.
A ginladi (bead mala) has beads in groups of 10. Slide beads to add.
On a number line, start at the first number and hop forward.
9 + 6: start at 9, hop 6, land on 15.

example.q: Use a mala to find 8 + 7.
steps: Slide 2 more to fill the ten. 5 are still to slide.

learn.reallife: Counting beads on a mala or seeds in a row helps us add big numbers.

quiz.q: 7 tomatoes and 5 more tomatoes. Fill in: 7 + 5 = ___
quiz.explain: 7 + 3 makes 10, then 2 more makes 12.

quiz.q: Start at 11 on the number line. Hop 6. Where do you land?
quiz.mistake: Counts the start as a hop

quiz.q: On a mala, Riya slides 9 beads and then 4 more. How many beads?
quiz.explain: 9 + 1 makes 10, then 3 more makes 13.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the bead used to make 10

quiz.q: Kabir starts at 13 and hops 5. Where does he land?
Which hops show 6 + 8?
quiz.explain: Start at one number, hop the other.
quiz.mistake: Uses the wrong number of hops

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find 9 + 5 on the number line?
teach.praise: Start at 9, hop 5, land on 14. Hop-tastic!
teach.nudge: Where do I start? How many hops?

learn.hook: Big numbers have a ten hiding inside! Use it to add fast.
points: 12 is 10 and 2. To add 12 + 6, first add the ones: 2 + 6 = 8.
There is often another way: count on 6 from 12: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18.
Talk with a friend. Both ways give the same answer.

example.q: Find 13 + 5 by splitting 13.

learn.reallife: ₹10 note and ₹3 in coins, plus ₹5 more: add the coins first, then the note.

quiz.q: What is 12 + 6?
14 + 3 is the same as 10 + ___.
quiz.explain: 4 ones + 3 ones = 7 ones.

quiz.q: Find 15 + 4.
Meena adds 11 + 5 by counting on. Arjun splits 11 into 10 and 1. Who is right?
quiz.explain: Both ways give 16. There is more than one good way.

quiz.q: How do we split 13 to add?
quiz.explain: 13 is 1 ten and 3 ones: 10 and 3.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 1 as one, not ten

quiz.q: Riya has 16 bindis. She gets 4 more. How many now?

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I find 12 + 7 using the ten inside 12?
teach.praise: 10 and 2, then 2 + 7 = 9, so 19! Smart split!
teach.nudge: What is 12 made of? A ten and how many ones?

learn.hook: Picnic time! How much food should we pack?
points: Read the story and find the numbers.
'In all' and 'altogether' tell us to add.
For a picnic, list the food: 6 puris, 5 idlis, 4 bananas.
With three numbers, add two first. Then add the third.

example.q: For a picnic: 6 puris and 8 sandwiches. How many things to eat?

learn.reallife: Before a trip, Mummy counts the food so everyone gets enough.

games.title: True or false?
items: With 3 kinds of food, add two first, then the third.

quiz.q: Aisha has 8 pencils. She buys 6 more. How many pencils now?
quiz.explain: 8 + 2 = 10, then 4 more makes 14.

quiz.q: Dadi makes 9 laddoos in the morning and 7 at night. How many laddoos?
quiz.explain: 9 + 1 = 10, then 6 more makes 16.

quiz.q: Riya wears 7 bangles on one hand and 5 on the other. How many bangles?
quiz.explain: 7 + 3 = 10, then 2 more makes 12.

quiz.q: For the picnic, Joseph packs 4 bananas, 5 oranges and 3 apples. How many fruits?
The picnic basket has 10 puris and 8 parathas. How many in all?
Which word in a story tells us to add?
quiz.explain: Altogether means put all together.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up add words and take-away words

teach.ask: Gappu: For our picnic I have 7 rotis and 6 idlis. How many things to eat?
teach.praise: 7 + 3 = 10, and 3 more is 13. Picnic ready!
teach.nudge: Is this an add story or a take-away story? Which numbers?

learn.hook: Rabbits nibbled some carrots! How many are left?
points: Count back to take away.
Or count up from the small number to the big one.
15 - 5 = 10. Take away the ones to reach 10.
Taking away makes the number smaller (unless we take away 0).

example.q: There are 14 cabbages. 6 are sold. How many are left?

learn.reallife: When sweets get eaten or toys get given away, we subtract.

games.title: Smallest to biggest answer
games.prompt: Order by the answer, smallest first

quiz.q: What is 15 - 5?
quiz.explain: Take away the 5 ones from 15. 10 is left.

quiz.q: What is 12 - 3?
quiz.explain: Take 2 to reach 10. Take 1 more: 9.

quiz.q: 17 brinjals grow. Riya picks 7. How many are still growing?
quiz.explain: 17 take away 7 is 10.

quiz.q: What is 20 - 8?
quiz.explain: Count up from 8 to 10 is 2. Then 10 more to 20. 2 + 10 = 12.

quiz.q: What is 14 - 9?
quiz.explain: Count up from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. That is 5.

quiz.q: Aisha has 16 beans. She plants 8. How many are left?

teach.ask: Gappu: I had 13 seeds. I ate 4. How do I find what is left?
teach.praise: Take 3 to reach 10, then 1 more. 9 seeds left!
teach.nudge: Do I count back? Can I stop at 10 on the way?

learn.hook: Draw a number strip on the floor. How many ways can you reach 12?
points: Draw a number strip from 0 to 20 on the floor with chalk.
Reach 12 in different ways: 10 + 2, 8 + 4, 15 - 3.
Many sums and take-aways can land on the same number.
Check each way by hopping it.

example.q: Find two ways to reach 14 on the strip.

learn.reallife: There are many roads to the same market. Numbers are like that too!

quiz.q: Which way reaches 15?
quiz.mistake: Does not work out each way

quiz.q: Riya starts at 9 and lands on 16. How many did she hop forward?
quiz.mistake: Counts the start as a hop

quiz.q: Kabir starts at 20 and hops back 3. Where does he land?
Which one does NOT land on 10?
Meena hops 8 + 5. Joseph hops 20 - 7. Do they land on the same number?
options: No, they land on different numbers
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding and taking away can't give the same number

quiz.q: Start at 11. How many hops forward to reach 19?
quiz.mistake: Counts the start as a hop

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to land on 11. Show me two different ways!
teach.praise: 10 + 1 and 12 - 1 both land on 11. Two roads, one home!
