teach.nudge: Can I add to reach 11? Can I take away to reach 11?

learn.hook: Every farm has a story. Let us solve them!
points: Read the story slowly.
Find the numbers.
Words like 'more come', 'in all', 'altogether' usually mean add.
Words like 'left', 'gave away', 'ate' usually mean take away.

example.q: Harpreet has 9 potatoes. Her dadi gives her 6 more. How many in all?
steps: 'More' and 'in all' tell us to add.

learn.reallife: At the sabzi market we count what we buy and what is left.

games.title: True or false?
items: In all asks for the total.
'How many are left' usually means we add.
Left means some went away. We take away.
10 hens and 5 more hens make 15 hens.

quiz.q: A farmer has 12 hens. 5 more come. How many hens in all?
quiz.explain: More come, so add. 12 + 5 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts when the story says more

quiz.q: There are 18 mangoes. A monkey takes 6. How many are left?
quiz.explain: Taken away, so subtract. 18 - 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds when the story says taken

quiz.q: Joseph plants 8 seeds on Monday and 9 on Tuesday. How many seeds altogether?
quiz.explain: Altogether means add. 8 + 9 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Makes a counting slip when adding

quiz.q: Meena has 15 cucumbers. She sells 9. How many are left?
quiz.explain: Sells means they go away. 15 - 9 = 6.

quiz.q: A cart has 10 pumpkins. 10 more are loaded. How many now?
quiz.explain: Loaded means more. 10 + 10 = 20.

quiz.q: Riya had 13 peas. A bird ate some. Now she has 8. How many did the bird eat?
quiz.explain: Count up from 8 to 13: that is 5.

teach.ask: Gappu: The story says 'how many are left'. Do I add?
teach.praise: Left means take away. In all means add. You are a star!
teach.nudge: Which words tell me to add? Which words tell me to take away?

topics.title: Two-step stories: diyas and the bus

learn.hook: Some stories have two parts. Solve one step, then the next!
points: Some stories have two steps. Do one step at a time.
Diyas: made 8, sold 5, made 6 more. 8 - 5 = 3. Then 3 + 6 = 9.
Bus: 10 children, 4 get on, 3 get off. 10 + 4 = 14. Then 14 - 3 = 11.
Getting on means add. Getting off means take away.

example.q: A bus has 12 children. 5 get off. Then 2 get on. How many now?

learn.reallife: Before Diwali, a potter makes diyas, sells some and makes more again.

games.title: Two-step story
games.prompt: Do these from first to last
items: Use that answer in the second step

items.text: Diyas: 4 are left, then 5 more are made. Now ___.

quiz.q: Potter Ramu made 8 diyas. He sold 5. Then he made 6 more. How many diyas now?
A bus has 10 children. 4 get on. Then 3 get off. How many now?
At a stop, 2 children get on the bus. Add or take away?
quiz.explain: Getting on means more children. We add.

quiz.q: Riya has 15 toffees. She eats 3. Mummy gives her 4. How many now?
A bus has 7 children. 6 get on. Then 5 get off. How many now?
Meena made 9 diyas and then 9 more. She sold 11. How many are left?

teach.ask: Gappu: My bus has 8 chicks. 5 get on, then 2 get off. How many now?
teach.praise: 8 + 5 = 13, then 13 - 2 = 11. Two steps done!
teach.nudge: What happens first? What do I do next?

learn.hook: Lina's whole family has come home! Who is taller than whom?
points: Count each family member once.
Lina is taller than baby Tinu but shorter than Papa. Lina is in between.
If A is taller than B, then B is shorter than A.
Compare with your own family: who is taller than you?
Stand back to back on a flat floor to compare.

example.q: Mummy is taller than Lina. Lina is taller than Tinu. Who is taller than Tinu but shorter than Mummy?
steps: Mummy is the tallest of the three.

learn.reallife: At school, we stand in a line from shortest to tallest for the assembly.

games.title: Shortest to tallest
games.prompt: Put them from shortest to tallest

games.title: True or false?
items: If Riya is taller than Kabir, then Kabir is shorter than Riya.
Taller one way means shorter the other way.
Lina is taller than Tinu and shorter than Papa. So Lina is the tallest.
To compare heights, stand back to back.
Then we can see whose head is higher.
We count each family member once.
Do not skip or count twice.

quiz.q: Lina's family: 👴👵👨👩👧👶. How many people?
quiz.explain: Count each one once: 1 to 6.

quiz.q: Mummy is taller than Lina. Lina is taller than Tinu. Who is in between?
quiz.explain: Lina is shorter than Mummy but taller than Tinu.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tallest instead of the middle

quiz.q: Arjun is taller than Riya but shorter than Dada. Who is the tallest?
quiz.explain: Dada is taller than Arjun, and Arjun is taller than Riya.

quiz.q: Meena is shorter than her brother. Who is taller?
quiz.explain: If Meena is shorter, her brother is taller.

quiz.q: Kabir and Joseph stand back to back. Kabir's head is higher. Who is taller?
quiz.explain: The higher head belongs to the taller child.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to read a back-to-back check

quiz.q: At the get-together, 3 cousins and 4 aunts and uncles came. How many came?
quiz.explain: 3 and 4 make 7.

teach.ask: Gappu: Papa bird is taller than me. I am taller than my baby sister. Where am I?
teach.praise: You are in between! Taller than baby, shorter than Papa.
teach.nudge: Am I the tallest, the shortest, or somewhere else?

learn.hook: Lina's family stands in a row for a photo. Who is the tallest?
points: Tall means high from feet to head.
Taller means more tall than another.
Tallest means more tall than everyone else.
Shortest means less tall than everyone else.
Stand on the same floor to compare heights.

example.q: Papa is taller than Lina. Lina is taller than baby Tinu. Who is the tallest?
steps: So Papa is taller than both.

learn.reallife: We line up by height in the school assembly. A coconut tree is taller than a rose plant.

games.title: Shortest to tallest
games.prompt: Put them from shortest to tallest

games.title: True or false?
items: A giraffe is taller than a goat.
A giraffe has very long legs and neck.
A baby is usually taller than her dadi.
A grown-up dadi is taller than a baby.
To compare heights, both should stand on the same floor.
A coconut tree is shorter than a tulsi plant.
A coconut tree is much taller.
If Riya is taller than Meena, Meena is shorter than Riya.

quiz.q: Who is taller?
quiz.explain: A grown-up is taller than a small baby.

quiz.q: Which is the tallest?
quiz.explain: A coconut tree grows very high. It is the tallest.

quiz.q: Arjun is taller than Kabir. Who is shorter?
quiz.explain: If Arjun is taller, Kabir must be shorter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks taller and shorter mean the same

quiz.q: Riya is taller than Aisha. Aisha is taller than Joseph. Who is the shortest?
quiz.explain: Riya is taller than Aisha. Aisha is taller than Joseph. So Joseph is the shortest.

quiz.q: Meena stands on a chair. Harpreet stands on the floor. Is it fair to compare their heights?
quiz.explain: No. Both must stand on the same floor to compare fairly.
quiz.mistake: Forgets both must start at the same level

quiz.q: Which is taller?
quiz.explain: A bus is much taller than a bicycle.

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend and I want to know who is taller. What should we do?
teach.praise: Stand back to back on the same floor. Then we can see!
teach.nudge: Where should we stand? Which word tells who is higher?

learn.hook: Which is closer to your home: the shop or the school?
points: Near means close. Far means a long way off.
Nearer means more near. Nearest means the most near of all.
Farther means more far. Farthest means the most far of all.
Count steps: fewer steps away means nearer.

example.q: The shop is 5 steps from Lina's house. The school is 20 steps. The bus stop is 12 steps. Which is nearest? Which is farthest?
example.answer: The shop is nearest, the school is farthest

learn.reallife: We walk to a nearby shop, but take a bus to a faraway city.

items.text: The shop is 5 steps away. The well is 9 steps away. The shop is ___.
Of 3, 8 and 15 steps away, 15 steps is the ___.
Of 6, 2 and 11 steps away, 2 steps is the ___.
The moon is ___ from us than the clouds.

quiz.q: Riya's house is 4 steps from the shop. Kabir's house is 9 steps. Whose house is nearer to the shop?
quiz.explain: 4 steps is fewer than 9 steps. Fewer steps means nearer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger number is nearer

quiz.q: School: 20 steps. Temple: 35 steps. Park: 10 steps. Which is nearest?
quiz.explain: 10 is the fewest steps.

quiz.q: Well: 6 steps. Shop: 15 steps. Bus stop: 3 steps. Which is farthest?
quiz.explain: 15 is the most steps.

quiz.q: Joseph walks 7 steps to the tap and 12 steps to the gate. How many more steps to the gate?
quiz.explain: 12 is 5 more than 7.

quiz.q: Which is farther from you: your nose or the moon?
quiz.explain: The moon is very far away in the sky.

quiz.q: Aisha is 3 steps from the bus. Meena is 8 steps. Harpreet is 5 steps. Who is nearest to the bus?
quiz.explain: 3 steps is the fewest.

teach.ask: Gappu: My nest is 3 hops from the tree and 9 hops from the pond. Which is nearer?
teach.praise: The tree is nearer: 3 hops is fewer than 9. The pond is farther!
teach.nudge: Which place takes fewer hops?

learn.hook: A tree trunk and a thread: one is thick, one is thin!
points: Line things up from the same starting end to compare lengths.
The one that goes farthest is the longest. The one that ends first is the shortest.
Thick means wide. Thin means narrow.
A tree trunk is thick. A thread is thin.

example.q: A rope, a ribbon and a thread start at one end. The ribbon ends last. The thread ends first. Which is longest? Which is shortest?
steps: They start at the same end, so it is fair.

learn.reallife: A belan is thick, a needle is thin. Tailors pick thin thread for sewing.

quiz.q: Which is the thickest?
quiz.explain: A tree trunk is very wide.

quiz.q: Which is the thinnest?
quiz.explain: A hair is the narrowest.

quiz.q: Three pencils start at the same end. The red one ends last. Which is the longest?
quiz.explain: The one that goes farthest is the longest.

quiz.q: Why do we line things up at one end before comparing lengths?
quiz.explain: With the same start, the end shows which is longer.

quiz.q: Which is the longest?
quiz.explain: A train has many coaches. It is the longest.

quiz.q: Strips made of the same blocks: green 6, blue 9, red 4. Which is the shortest?
quiz.explain: 4 blocks is the fewest, so red is shortest.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have a twig and a thread. How do I check which is longer? Which is thicker?
teach.praise: Line them up at one end! The twig is thicker too. Smart!
teach.nudge: Where should both things start? Which one is wider?

learn.hook: No ruler? No problem! Use your hands and feet.
points: A handspan is from thumb tip to little finger tip, spread wide.
We can measure a table in handspans.
We can measure a room in footsteps.
We can measure a book with paper clips or erasers.
Count how many fit from one end to the other.

example.q: Kabir puts erasers in a line along his pencil box. 6 erasers fit. How long is it?

learn.reallife: Mummy measures cloth with her arm. We count steps from class to the gate.

items.text: Put clips end to end with no ___.
Riya uses her hand. Table A is 5 handspans. Table B is 7. Table B is ___.
A handspan is measured with your ___.

quiz.q: Riya measures two desks with her hand. The red desk is 4 handspans. The blue desk is 6. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: 6 of her handspans is more than 4. So the blue desk is longer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a smaller count means longer

quiz.q: A pencil is 5 paper clips long. How many clips fit along it?
quiz.explain: 5 clips long means 5 clips fit end to end.

quiz.q: Which is best to measure the length of a classroom?
quiz.explain: A classroom is big. Footsteps are quicker for big things.
quiz.mistake: Picks a tiny unit for a big thing

quiz.q: Meena measures her book with blocks: 🟦🟦🟦. How many blocks long?
quiz.explain: Count the blocks: 1, 2, 3.

quiz.q: Aisha measures two mats with her hand. The green mat is 8 handspans. The red is 5. How many more is green?
quiz.explain: 8 - 5 = 3. The green mat is 3 handspans longer.

quiz.q: Joseph measures a rope. He leaves big gaps between his clips. Is his answer right?
options: No, there should be no gaps
quiz.explain: Clips must touch end to end. Gaps give a wrong count.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have no ruler. How can I find how long my nest is?
teach.praise: Use handspans end to end and count them. Brilliant!
teach.nudge: What can I use instead of a ruler? Do I count them?

topics.title: Guess, choose a unit and measure

learn.hook: Guess first! Then measure. Who will guess closest?
points: Measure your arm in handspans, from shoulder to fingertips.
A friend's arm may give a different count.
Use handspans for big things, like a table. Use finger widths for small things, like an eraser.
First guess how many. Then measure. Was your guess close?

example.q: Riya guesses her desk is 5 handspans long. She measures 7. How many more than her guess?

learn.reallife: Dadi guesses how much atta she needs, then checks with a cup.

games.title: True or false?
items: Finger widths are best to measure a bed.
A bed is big. Use handspans.
My arm and my friend's arm may give different counts.
Arms and hands are not the same size.
A guess must always be exactly right.
A guess is a good try. Then we measure.

quiz.q: Which is best measured with finger widths?
quiz.explain: An eraser is small. Finger widths fit it well.
quiz.mistake: Uses a small unit for a big thing

quiz.q: Which is best measured with handspans?
quiz.explain: A table is big. Handspans are quicker.
quiz.mistake: Uses a big unit for a tiny thing

quiz.q: Kabir guesses 6 handspans. He measures 8. How many more than his guess?
quiz.explain: 8 is 2 more than 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds the guess and the measure

quiz.q: Meena's arm is 3 of her handspans. Aisha's arm is 4 of her handspans. Can both be right?
options: Yes, hands and arms are different sizes
quiz.explain: Different hands and arms give different counts.

quiz.q: Joseph guesses a book is 10 finger widths. He measures 7. Was his guess more or less?
quiz.explain: 10 is more than 7.

quiz.q: What should you do first?
quiz.explain: We guess first, then measure to check.
quiz.mistake: Skips the guessing or the measuring

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to measure a matchbox. Should I use handspans or finger widths? What do I do first?
teach.praise: Finger widths for small things. Guess first, then measure!
teach.nudge: Is a matchbox big or small? What comes before measuring?

learn.hook: Papa and Lina measure the same mat. They get different answers! Why?
points: Big hands give a smaller count.
Small hands give a bigger count.
Papa's handspan is bigger than Lina's.
To compare, use the same thing to measure.

example.q: Papa measures a table: 5 handspans. Lina measures it: 8 handspans. Why?
steps: Papa's hand is bigger, so fewer fit.
Lina's hand is smaller, so more fit.
example.answer: Lina's hand is smaller, so she counts more.

learn.reallife: Tailors use one measuring tape so everyone gets the same answer.

games.title: True or false?
items: A bigger hand gives a smaller count.
Fewer big hands fit along the same thing.
Papa and Lina will always get the same handspan count.
Using the same clips helps us compare fairly.
A small foot takes fewer steps across a room.
Measuring with one tape gives everyone the same answer.
The tape does not change size.

quiz.q: Dada and Riya measure the same rug with footsteps. Who takes more steps?
quiz.explain: Riya's feet are smaller. More small steps fit.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger feet need more steps

quiz.q: Papa's table is 6 of his handspans. Lina gets 9 of her handspans. Who has the bigger hand?
quiz.explain: Fewer handspans fit, so Papa's hand is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger count means a bigger hand

quiz.q: A rope is 4 pencils long. It is also ___ clips long.
quiz.explain: A clip is smaller than a pencil. More clips fit along the rope.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the count stays the same with any unit

quiz.q: Arjun and Kabir must compare their desks fairly. What should they do?
quiz.explain: Using the same unit makes the comparison fair.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why the unit must be the same

quiz.q: A stick is 3 big erasers long. Harpreet measures it with small erasers. Which count can be right?

quiz.mistake: Picks a smaller count for a smaller unit

quiz.q: Meena's book is 7 clips long. Aisha's book is 7 clips long, with the same clips. What is true?
quiz.explain: Same clips, same count. So the books are the same length.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two lengths can never be equal

teach.ask: Gappu: My mama and I measured our nest. We got different numbers! Who is wrong?
teach.praise: Nobody was wrong! Bigger hands count less. Use the same thing to be fair.
teach.nudge: Are our hands the same size? What should we both use?

learn.hook: A feather and a brick: which one pulls your hand down?
points: Heavy things are hard to lift. Light things are easy to lift.
Heavier means more heavy. Lighter means less heavy.
Hold one thing in each hand. The hand pulled down more has the heavier thing.
A big thing is not always heavier. A balloon is big but light.
We check our weight on a weighing machine, at home or at a clinic.

example.q: Lina holds a brick in one hand and a feather in the other. Which is heavier?
steps: The brick hand is pulled down.

learn.reallife: At the market, vegetables are weighed on a scale.

games.title: True or false?
items: A big balloon is heavier than a small stone.
The balloon is big but very light.
The hand that goes down more holds the heavier thing.
A feather is lighter than a book.
A feather is very easy to lift.
A pumpkin is lighter than a grape.
A weighing machine tells how heavy we are.
Doctors use one at the clinic.

quiz.q: Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: A watermelon is much harder to lift.

quiz.q: Which is lighter?
quiz.explain: A leaf is very easy to lift.

quiz.q: Kabir holds a book and a pencil. His book hand goes down. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: The hand pulled down holds the heavier thing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hand that stays up is heavier

quiz.q: Which is true?
options: A big balloon can be lighter than a small stone
quiz.explain: Size does not always tell weight.

quiz.q: Riya weighs 20 kg. Her brother weighs 15 kg. Who is heavier?
quiz.explain: 20 is more than 15.

quiz.q: Where can we check how heavy we are?
quiz.explain: A weighing machine shows weight.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up weight with length or time

teach.ask: Gappu: I hold a pebble and a feather. How do I know which is heavier?
teach.praise: The pebble pulls your wing down. It is heavier! The feather is lighter.
teach.nudge: What happens to the hand with the heavier thing?

learn.hook: How many mugs fill a bucket? Let us count and splash!
points: Fill a bucket with mugs of water. Count the mugs.
A bucket that takes more mugs holds more.
Use the same cup to fill bottles. More cups means it holds more.
We need a lot of water for a bath and only a little to drink.

example.q: Bucket A takes 8 mugs. Bucket B takes 5 mugs. Which holds more? By how many mugs?
steps: 8 is more than 5, so Bucket A holds more.

learn.reallife: Saving water: use a bucket for a bath instead of a running shower.

games.title: A little or a lot of water?

items.text: A bottle takes 4 cups. A jug takes 7 cups. The ___ holds more.
A spoon holds ___ water than a bucket.
A tub takes 9 mugs and a bucket takes 6. The tub holds ___ more mugs.
For a bath we need ___ water.

quiz.q: One bucket is filled with 7 mugs. Another needs 10 mugs. How many more mugs for the second?
quiz.explain: 10 is 3 more than 7.

quiz.q: Which holds the most water?
quiz.explain: A bucket is the biggest container here.

quiz.q: Using the same cup, a bottle takes 5 cups and a jug takes 8. Which holds less?
quiz.explain: 5 cups is less than 8 cups.

quiz.q: Which needs the most water?
quiz.explain: A bath needs a whole bucket of water.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how much water a task needs

quiz.q: Kabir fills a pot using 4 glasses. Then he fills a second pot the same way. How many glasses in all?
quiz.explain: 4 and 4 make 8.

quiz.q: Why must we use the same cup to compare two bottles?
quiz.explain: Different cups hold different amounts, so counts would not match.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why the unit must be the same

teach.praise: The cup holds more: 6 spoons beat 3! Splash!
teach.nudge: How many spoons for each? Which number is bigger?

learn.hook: Twenty is not the end! Let us count on to thirty.
points: We read 21 as twenty-one and 30 as thirty.
To count many neem leaves or flowers, make groups of ten first, then count on.

example.q: Meena has 2 bunches of 10 flowers and 4 loose flowers. How many flowers?

learn.reallife: A month has about 30 days. Look at the dates on a calendar!

quiz.q: Count the neem leaves: 🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃🍃
quiz.explain: Make two tens (20), then count on 21, 22, 23.
quiz.mistake: Loses count in a big group

quiz.q: What comes just after 29?
quiz.explain: After 29 comes 30.

quiz.q: How do we write 'twenty-six'?
quiz.explain: Twenty is 2 tens, six is 6 ones: 26.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the wrong order

quiz.q: Riya has 2 bunches of 10 flowers and 5 more. How many flowers?
quiz.explain: 20 and 5 make 25.
After 25 comes 26.

quiz.q: Which number is twenty-eight?
quiz.explain: Twenty-eight is 2 tens and 8 ones: 28.

teach.ask: Gappu: I counted 20 seeds. Then I found 3 more. What number is it, and how do I say it?
teach.praise: 20, then 21, 22, 23. Twenty-three seeds!
teach.nudge: What comes after 20? Keep counting.

learn.hook: Counting big piles one by one is slow. Count in tens!
points: Each step adds one more ten.
3 tens is 30. 5 tens is 50.
Ten tens make 100!

example.q: Joseph has 4 packets. Each packet has 10 toffees. How many toffees?

learn.reallife: Shops pack biscuits and pencils in tens. ₹10 notes are counted in tens too.

quiz.q: What is 6 tens?
quiz.explain: Count in tens 6 times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.

quiz.q: Count in tens: 30, 40, ___, 60. What is missing?
quiz.explain: Each step adds one ten. After 40 comes 50.

quiz.q: Riya has 3 bundles of 10 sticks. How many sticks?
quiz.explain: 10, 20, 30. Three tens make 30.

quiz.q: How many tens make 80?
quiz.mistake: Gives the whole number instead of the tens

quiz.q: What comes after 90 when counting in tens?
quiz.explain: 90 and one more ten make 100.

quiz.q: Kabir has 2 packs of 10 pencils. How many pencils?
quiz.explain: 10, 20. Two tens make 20.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have a big pile of seeds. How can I count them fast?
teach.praise: Make groups of ten and count 10, 20, 30! So quick!
teach.nudge: Can I make groups? How many in each group?

learn.hook: Every big number has a tens part and a ones part!
points: In 34, the 3 means 3 tens. The 4 means 4 ones.
3 tens and 4 ones make 30 + 4 = 34.
The left digit shows tens. The right digit shows ones.
45 and 54 are different numbers!

example.q: Aisha has 5 bundles of ten sticks and 2 loose sticks. What number is this?

learn.reallife: ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins show tens and ones. Three ₹10 notes and five ₹1 coins make ₹35.

quiz.q: What number is 3 tens and 6 ones?
quiz.explain: 3 tens is 30. 30 and 6 make 36.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and the ones

quiz.explain: In 72, the 7 is the tens digit. So 7 tens.

quiz.q: How many ones are in 49?
quiz.explain: In 49, the 9 is the ones digit.

quiz.q: Meena has ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins. 2 notes and 5 coins. How much?

quiz.explain: 8 tens is 80. No ones, so 80.

quiz.q: Harpreet makes 2 tens and 3 ones with sticks. What number?
quiz.explain: 2 tens is 20. 20 and 3 make 23.

teach.ask: Gappu: What does the 2 mean in 25? Is it just two?
teach.praise: The 2 means 2 tens, that is 20! The 5 means 5 ones!
teach.nudge: Is the 2 tens or ones? What about the 5?

learn.hook: Fill frame after frame! How many dots make 50?
points: Ten frames show a number: 3 full frames and 4 more show 34.
5 full ten frames show 50.

example.q: Show 42 with ten frames.
steps: Put 2 dots in the next frame.

learn.reallife: Egg trays and chocolate boxes are like ten frames.

quiz.q: How many full ten frames show 40?
quiz.explain: 40 is 4 tens, so 4 full frames.

quiz.q: 3 full ten frames and 8 more dots. What number is it?
quiz.explain: 30 and 8 make 38.

quiz.q: Which number comes just after 49?
quiz.explain: After 49 comes 50.

quiz.q: To show 45, how many dots go in the frame that is not full?
quiz.explain: 45 is 4 full frames and 5 more.

quiz.q: Count the beads: 3 strings of 10 and 6 loose beads.
quiz.explain: 30 and 6 make 36.

quiz.q: Which number is forty-three?
quiz.explain: Forty is 4 tens, three is 3 ones: 43.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I show 35 with ten frames?
teach.praise: 3 full frames and 5 more dots. That is 35!
teach.nudge: How many tens are in 35? How many ones?

learn.hook: Clip, clip, clip! Can you put every card in the right spot on the string?
points: A ginladi is a string number line. We clip number cards on it in order.
Each card goes just after the number before it.
Card 25 goes between 24 and 26.
Read the cards from left to right: each one is 1 more.

example.q: Cards 31 and 33 are clipped on the string. Where does card 32 go?

learn.reallife: Seat numbers in a cinema hall or train coach go in order like a ginladi.

items.text: On the string, 35 is just left of ___.

quiz.q: Where does card 28 go on the string?
quiz.explain: 28 is 1 more than 27 and 1 less than 29.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the ones digit

quiz.q: Riya reads the cards: 41, 42, ___, 44. Which card is missing?
quiz.explain: After 42 comes 43.

quiz.q: Which card goes just before 30?
quiz.explain: Just before 30 is 29.

quiz.q: Kabir clipped 47 between 46 and 48. Is he right?
quiz.explain: 46, 47, 48 is the counting order.
quiz.mistake: Does not check the numbers on both sides

quiz.q: A card says forty-nine. Which card is it?
quiz.explain: Forty-nine is 4 tens and 9 ones: 49.

quiz.q: If we go on after 50, which card comes next?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 50 is 51.
quiz.mistake: Jumps by ten instead of one

teach.ask: Gappu: I have card 38. Where do I clip it on the string?
teach.praise: Between 37 and 39! Clip!
teach.nudge: Which card comes just before 38? Which comes after?

learn.hook: A number chart is like a map of numbers! Find the missing ones.
points: To count up to 50 things, make tens first, then count the ones.
A number chart has rows of ten: 1 to 10, 11 to 20, 21 to 30, and so on.
Going right, each number is 1 more. Going down, each number is 10 more.

learn.reallife: Classroom roll numbers, house numbers and calendar dates follow this order.

items.text: The number just right of 38 is ___.

quiz.explain: 40 and 7 make 47.
After 37 comes 38.

quiz.mistake: Loses count in a big group

quiz.explain: It goes down by 1. After 48 comes 47.

quiz.q: What is missing: 20, 30, ___, 50?
quiz.explain: It goes up by 10. 30 + 10 = 40.

teach.ask: Gappu: In the chart, which number is just below 26?
teach.praise: Down one row adds 10. 26 + 10 = 36!
teach.nudge: What happens to the number when I move down a row?

learn.hook: Dadi sews tiny mirrors on a dupatta. So many! How do we count them?
points: In 73, the 7 means 7 tens and the 3 means 3 ones.
To count a big collection, like mirrors on a dupatta, make groups of ten.
99 is the biggest 2-digit number. After 99 comes 100.

example.q: Dadi sews mirrors in groups of 10. She makes 6 groups and 3 more mirrors. How many mirrors?

learn.reallife: Mirror work is a craft from Gujarat and Rajasthan. Count the mirrors on a bag or a dupatta!

quiz.explain: Eighty is 8 tens, five is 5 ones: 85.

quiz.q: What comes just after 59?
quiz.explain: After 59 comes 60.

teach.ask: Gappu: I counted 99 grains. One more falls in. How many now?
teach.praise: 99 and one more is 100. Hooray for a hundred!
teach.nudge: What comes just after 99?

learn.hook: Let us explore numbers all the way up to 99!
points: After 29 comes 30. After 39 comes 40.
To find the bigger number, look at the tens first.
If the tens are the same, look at the ones.
99 is the biggest 2-digit number.

example.q: Which is bigger: 47 or 52?

learn.reallife: House numbers, bus numbers and cricket scores go past 20.

quiz.q: What comes just after 39?
quiz.explain: After 9 ones, we get a new ten. 39 then 40.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the tens stay the same

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 64 or 46?
quiz.explain: 64 has 6 tens. 46 has 4 tens. 6 tens is more.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit first

quiz.explain: Tens are the same (8). Ones: 3 is less than 7. So 83 is smaller.

quiz.q: What comes just before 60?
quiz.explain: Count back one from 60: 59.

quiz.q: Which number is between 77 and 79?
quiz.explain: 77, 78, 79. 78 is in between.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two

quiz.q: Arjun scores 58 runs. Kabir scores 85 runs. Who scored more?
quiz.explain: 85 has 8 tens. 58 has 5 tens. 85 is more.

teach.ask: Gappu: Is 38 bigger than 83? They have the same digits!
teach.praise: Look at the tens first! 83 has 8 tens, so it is bigger!
teach.nudge: Which digit should I look at first? Which has more tens?

learn.hook: A long string with cards 1 to 99! Play with friends and put them in order.
points: Clip cards 1 to 99 on a long string. Friends take turns.
To order numbers, look at the tens first.
If the tens are the same, look at the ones.
Smallest to largest: 19, 45, 54, 91.

example.q: Put 63, 36 and 60 in order, smallest first.
steps: Tens: 6, 3, 6. 36 has the fewest tens, so it is smallest.
60 and 63 both have 6 tens. Ones: 0 is less than 3.

learn.reallife: In a race list, runners are put in order of their numbers.

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 72, 27, 70?
quiz.explain: 27 has only 2 tens.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit first

quiz.q: Put 81, 18, 58 from smallest to largest. Which is in the middle?
quiz.explain: In order: 18, 58, 81.

quiz.q: Which comes later on the string: 64 or 46?
quiz.explain: 64 has 6 tens. 46 has 4 tens. 64 is bigger, so it comes later.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit first

quiz.q: Which list of cards is in order, smallest first?
Kabir clips card 75. Which card is just before it?
quiz.explain: 1 less than 75 is 74.

quiz.q: Which is the biggest: 89, 98, 90?
quiz.explain: 98 has 9 tens and 8 ones. 90 has 9 tens and 0 ones.

teach.ask: Gappu: Which is bigger, 47 or 74? How do I know?
teach.praise: 74 has 7 tens. 47 has only 4 tens. So 74 is bigger!
teach.nudge: Which digit do I look at first?

learn.hook: Roll the dice, climb a ladder, slide down... reach 100 to win!
points: A board game has squares numbered 1 to 100, in rows of 10.
Roll a dice and move forward that many squares.
A ladder takes you up to a bigger number. A slide takes you back to a smaller one.
Fill missing squares by counting on from the number before.

learn.reallife: Snakes and Ladders (Moksha Patam) is an old Indian board game.

items.text: A slide from 54 down to 31 takes you ___.

quiz.explain: 25 is smaller than 46, so she went back.

quiz.explain: After 88 comes 89.

quiz.mistake: Counts the square she is on

teach.ask: Gappu: I am on square 45 and I roll ⚂. Where do I go?
teach.praise: 46, 47, 48! Gappu lands on 48!
teach.nudge: How many dots on ⚂? Count on from 45.

learn.hook: Circles, triangles and lines make dancing people! Welcome to Warli art.
points: Warli is a folk art from Maharashtra.
Warli pictures use circles, triangles and lines, in white on a brown wall.
A person has a circle head, a body of two triangles and line arms and legs.
We can count the houses, people and trees in a Warli picture.
For many tiny lines, guess first. Then count to check.

example.q: A Warli picture has 3 houses and 8 people dancing. How many houses and people in all?

learn.reallife: Many Indian walls, bags and cushion covers have Warli designs. Look for them!

items: It is a folk art of Maharashtra.

Simple shapes make the whole picture.
In Warli, a person's head is a square.
A guess must be the exact count.
A guess is a close try. We count to check.

White paint on a mud-brown wall.

quiz.q: Warli art comes from which state?
quiz.explain: Warli is a folk art of Maharashtra.

quiz.explain: Count each hut once: 4.

quiz.explain: 6 and 3 make 9.

quiz.explain: The head is a small circle.

quiz.explain: 24 is 4 more than 20.

quiz.explain: 1 and 2 make 3.

A pattern keeps the same order every time.

learn.hook: Doorsteps bloom with dots and lines! Let us make a kolam.

A kolam is drawn with rice flour around a grid of dots.
Many kolams look the same on both sides, like butterfly wings.
To complete one, copy one side onto the other side.
Rangoli colours and shapes often repeat around the centre.

Sarees, curtains and floor tiles have repeating designs too.
Look for the part that repeats.

chapters.title: How do I Spend my Day?

learn.hook: Things in a day happen in order. What comes first?
points: First we wake up. Next we brush. Then we eat breakfast.
We use words like first, next, then and last.
Before means earlier. After means later.
Some things must happen before others.

example.q: Put in order: eat breakfast, wake up, go to school.
example.answer: Wake up, eat breakfast, go to school

learn.reallife: Making chai has an order: boil water, add tea leaves, add milk, then pour.

games.title: True or false?
items: We wear shoes before we wear socks.
Socks go on first, then shoes.
We wash hands before we eat.
We dry ourselves after a bath.
First the bath, then we dry off.
We brush our teeth after we wake up.
First we wake up, then we brush.
We eat a mango before we peel it.
We peel or cut it first, then eat.

quiz.q: What do we do first?
quiz.explain: Socks go on first. Then shoes. Then we run!

quiz.q: Kabir plants a seed. What happens next?
quiz.explain: After planting, we water the seed. The tree grows much later.

quiz.q: Meena eats dinner, then brushes her teeth, then sleeps. What does she do last?
quiz.explain: Sleeping is the last thing in her list.

quiz.q: Which happens before lunch?
quiz.explain: Breakfast is in the morning. Lunch comes after it.

quiz.q: Aisha makes a sandwich. What does she do first?
quiz.explain: She needs bread first. She eats later.

quiz.explain: After coming home, he washes up. The others happen in the morning.

teach.praise: Socks first, then shoes! Order matters. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What should come first? What comes after?

learn.hook: Pihu has a busy day! Let us follow her from morning to night.
points: Morning: Pihu wakes up, exercises, brushes her teeth, takes a bath and eats breakfast.
Day: she goes to school, eats lunch with friends and rests.
Evening: she plays and does her homework.
Night: she eats dinner, reads a story and sleeps.

example.q: Pihu brushes her teeth and eats breakfast. Which does she do first?
steps: We brush our teeth soon after waking up.
Breakfast comes after brushing and bath.

learn.reallife: Your day has a morning, a school time, an evening and a night too!

quiz.q: Which does Pihu do in the morning?
quiz.explain: Pihu exercises after waking up in the morning.

quiz.explain: Lunch is in the middle of the day, at school.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parts of the day

quiz.q: What does Pihu do last at night?
quiz.explain: She sleeps after dinner and a story.

quiz.q: Which comes first in the morning?
quiz.explain: We must wake up before doing anything else.

quiz.q: Pihu plays in the park. The sun is going down. When is it?
quiz.explain: The sun goes down in the evening.

learn.hook: What do you do every single day? That is your routine!

example.answer: Wake up, brush teeth, bath, breakfast

learn.reallife: A good routine keeps us healthy and on time for school.

learn.hook: The sun rises, the sun sets. Our day has parts!
points: Morning: the sun comes up. We wake up and go to school.
Afternoon: the sun is high. We eat lunch.
Evening: the sun goes down. We play outside.
Night: it is dark. We see the moon and sleep.

example.q: Riya sees the moon and stars. She goes to bed. What part of the day is it?
steps: Moon and stars come out when it is dark.
We sleep when it is dark.

quiz.explain: Lunch time, with the sun high, is the afternoon.

learn.hook: Some jobs are quick. Some take a long time!
points: Blinking takes a very short time.
Brushing teeth takes a few minutes.
A school day takes many hours.
Growing a mango tree takes years!

A cricket match takes many hours.

quiz.q: Which takes more time?

quiz.explain: A blink is as quick as a clap.

quiz.explain: Making rangoli takes a long time. Opening a door is quick.

learn.hook: Hot sun, heavy rain, cold mornings! Why does the weather change?
points: India has seasons: summer, monsoon (rainy), winter and spring.
Summer is hot. We wear cotton clothes and use fans.
In the monsoon it rains a lot. We need umbrellas and raincoats.
Winter is cold. We wear sweaters. Spring brings new leaves and flowers.

steps: Umbrellas and raincoats keep us dry.
We need them when it rains a lot.

games.title: Summer or winter?
items: Sitting in the sun to keep warm

points: 3 groups of 2 is 2 + 2 + 2.
We can skip count: 2, 4, 6.
4 groups of 5 is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

example.q: Kabir has 3 packets. Each has 5 toffees. How many toffees?

learn.reallife: A cricket team gets 2 runs, 2 runs, 2 runs. That is repeated addition!

quiz.q: What is 3 + 3 + 3?
quiz.explain: 3, 6, 9. Three 3s make 9.

quiz.q: 4 groups of 2 is the same as ___.
quiz.explain: 4 groups of 2 means add 2 four times.
quiz.mistake: Adds the number of groups and the group size

quiz.q: Meena has 2 plates with 5 idlis each. How many idlis?
Skip count by 2: 2, 4, 6, ___. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 2. 6 + 2 = 8.

quiz.q: 5 children each hold 2 balloons. How many balloons?
Harpreet has 3 rows of 4 stickers. How many stickers?

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 nests with 2 eggs each. How do I find all the eggs?
teach.praise: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. I have 6 eggs!
teach.nudge: How many eggs in each nest? Do I add them again and again?

learn.hook: Cheenu goes shopping. Everything comes in packs!
points: Erasers come in packs of 2. 4 packs: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. 4 times 2 is 8.
Pencils come in packs of 3. 5 packs: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 15. 5 times 3 is 15.
Apples come in bags of 3. 3 bags: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. 3 times 3 is 9.
Count the packs, then count the things in one pack.

example.q: Cheenu buys 5 packs of pencils. Each pack has 3 pencils. How many pencils?
steps: Skip count by 3, once for each pack.

learn.reallife: Biscuits, soaps and pencils are sold in packs. Counting packs is faster!

quiz.q: Cheenu buys 4 packs of erasers. Each pack has 2. How many erasers?
5 packs of pencils, 3 in each pack. How many pencils?
3 bags of apples, 3 in each bag. How many apples?
Which sentence is right for 4 packs of 2?
quiz.explain: 4 packs is 4 groups. 2 in each. 4 times 2 is 8.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the number of packs and the number in a pack

quiz.q: Cheenu buys 2 bags of 5 bananas. How many bananas?
Cheenu counts by packs of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12. How many packs did he count?
quiz.explain: He said 4 numbers, one for each pack.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead of the packs

teach.ask: Gappu: I bought 3 packs of seeds. Each pack has 2 seeds. How many seeds?
teach.praise: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. 3 times 2 is 6 seeds!
teach.nudge: How many seeds in one pack? How many packs?

learn.hook: Let us go to the market! First, let us know our money.
points: Our money is the rupee. We write ₹.
Coins are round and made of metal: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10.
Notes are made of paper: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100.
A ₹5 coin is worth five ₹1 coins.

example.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹5?

learn.reallife: We pay with coins and notes at the sabzi market and the sweet shop.

games.title: Smallest to biggest
games.prompt: Put money in order, least first

quiz.q: Which is worth the most?
quiz.explain: 5 is more than 2 and 1. So ₹5 is worth the most.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger-looking coin is worth more

quiz.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹2?
quiz.mistake: Thinks one coin of any kind is the same

quiz.q: Which one is a note, not a coin?
quiz.explain: ₹100 comes as a paper note. ₹1 and ₹2 are coins.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which money is paper

quiz.q: Riya has two ₹5 coins. How much money is that?
How many ₹10 notes make ₹20?
quiz.explain: ₹10 + ₹10 = ₹20. That is 2 notes.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the value with the number of notes

quiz.q: What sign do we use for rupees?
quiz.explain: ₹ is the sign for our rupee.

teach.ask: Gappu: My shiny coin and a paper note. Which is money?
teach.praise: Both! Coins and notes are both rupees. Wow!
teach.nudge: Are coins money? Are notes money too? What do we call our money?

learn.hook: Rahim Kaka sells toys! Do you have enough money?
points: Rahim Kaka's toys have price tags: a whistle ₹5, a ball ₹10, a doll ₹14.
Four ₹5 coins make ₹20: 5, 10, 15, 20.
Two ₹10 notes make ₹20.
If a toy costs ₹14 and you have ₹10, you need ₹4 more.
With ₹30, pick toys whose prices add up to ₹30 or less.

example.q: A doll costs ₹14. Sara has ₹10. How much more does she need?

learn.reallife: At a mela, we check our money before choosing a toy.

items.text: Toy ₹14, I have ₹10. I need ₹___ more.
Toy ₹18, I have ₹10. I need ₹___ more.

games.title: True or false?
items: With ₹30 you can buy a ₹10 ball and a ₹20 kite.
With ₹30 you can buy a ₹20 kite and a ₹15 drum.

quiz.q: How many ₹5 coins make ₹20?
quiz.explain: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 coins.

quiz.q: A kite costs ₹20. Ravi pays only with ₹10 notes. How many notes does he give?
A toy car costs ₹17. Sara has ₹10. How much more does she need?
quiz.explain: Count up from 10 to 17: that is ₹7.
quiz.mistake: Adds the price and the money

quiz.q: A drum costs ₹19. Kabir has ₹15. How much more does he need?
quiz.explain: 15 + 4 = 19. He needs ₹4 more.

quiz.q: Meena and Aisha have ₹30 together. Which two toys can they buy?
quiz.explain: 10 + 20 = 30. The others cost ₹35 and ₹33, too much.
quiz.mistake: Does not add the two prices

quiz.q: Ball ₹10, whistle ₹5, top ₹12. You have ₹30. Can you buy all three?
quiz.explain: 10 + 5 + 12 = 27. That is less than 30.
quiz.mistake: Does not add all three prices

teach.ask: Gappu: A toy costs ₹15. I have ₹10. Can I buy it? How much more do I need?
teach.praise: Not yet! You need ₹5 more. Save up, Gappu!
teach.nudge: Is ₹10 as much as ₹15? Count up from 10 to 15.

learn.hook: At the mela, toys have prices. Can we buy them?
points: The price tells how much a thing costs.
If we have enough money, we can buy it.
If we pay more, we get some money back. That is change.
Change = money given - price.

example.q: A balloon costs ₹7. Riya pays ₹10. How much change?

learn.reallife: At the sweet shop, the shopkeeper gives back change when we pay more.

games.title: True or false?
items: With ₹10, Arjun can buy a ₹8 toy.
With ₹5, Meena can buy a ₹9 book.
₹5 is less than ₹9. Not enough money.
Pay ₹10 for a ₹4 ball. Change is ₹6.
Pay ₹20 for a ₹12 cap. Change is ₹12.
If you pay the exact price, you get no change.

quiz.q: A pencil costs ₹5. Kabir pays ₹10. How much change?
quiz.mistake: Adds the price to the money paid

quiz.q: A laddoo costs ₹8. Aisha has ₹6. Can she buy it?
quiz.explain: ₹6 is less than ₹8. She needs ₹2 more.

quiz.q: A toy car costs ₹13. Joseph pays ₹20. How much change?
quiz.explain: Count up from 13 to 20: that is 7.

quiz.q: Riya buys a ₹4 eraser and a ₹5 pencil. How much does she spend?
Riya pays ₹10 for things worth ₹9. How much change?
Arjun has ₹15. Which can he buy?
quiz.explain: ₹12 is less than ₹15. The others cost more than he has.
quiz.mistake: Picks a price higher than his money

teach.ask: Gappu: The kite costs ₹6. I gave ₹10. Why did I get money back?
teach.praise: I paid more than the price, so I get ₹4 change!
teach.nudge: Did I pay more than the price? How do I find the change?

learn.hook: Arjun has a few coins. How much money does he have?
points: Add the value of each coin or note.
Start with the biggest one. Count on.
Different coins can make the same amount.

example.q: Meena has a ₹10 coin, a ₹5 coin and a ₹2 coin. How much in all?

learn.reallife: We count money in our piggy bank. Shopkeepers count the money we give.

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹10 and ₹2. How much in all?
Aisha has three ₹2 coins. How much money?
quiz.mistake: Counts the coins, not their value

quiz.q: Which makes ₹10?
Harpreet has a ₹10 note, a ₹5 coin and a ₹1 coin. How much?
Joseph has ₹20 and Riya has ₹10. How much together?
Meena has 4 coins: ₹5, ₹5, ₹2, ₹1. How much?
quiz.mistake: Counts the coins instead of adding their values

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 coins. So I have ₹3, right?
teach.praise: Oh! Each coin has its own value. I must add them up!
teach.nudge: Is every coin worth ₹1? What should I add?

learn.hook: Can 1 coin do the work of 5 coins? Yes! Let us see how.
points: ₹10 can be one ₹10 coin, two ₹5 coins or five ₹2 coins.
To use the fewest coins, start with the biggest coin that fits.
₹7 with the fewest coins: ₹5 + ₹2. That is 2 coins.
Two groups match if they have the same total, even with different coins.

example.q: Make ₹8 with the fewest coins. You have ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10 coins.
steps: ₹10 is too big. Take ₹5. ₹3 is left.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers give change with the fewest coins so their coin box does not run out.

quiz.q: What is the fewest number of coins that make ₹10?
quiz.explain: One ₹10 coin is enough.
quiz.mistake: Uses smaller coins when one big coin fits

quiz.q: Make ₹9 with the fewest coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10). How many coins?
quiz.explain: ₹5 + ₹2 + ₹2 = ₹9. That is 3 coins.

quiz.q: Which group has the same value as ₹10?
quiz.mistake: Counts coins instead of adding their values

quiz.q: Riya has ₹5 + ₹5 + ₹5. Kabir has ₹10 + ₹5. What is true?
quiz.mistake: Thinks more coins means more money

quiz.q: Make ₹12 with the fewest coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10). How many coins?
quiz.explain: ₹10 + ₹2 = ₹12. Just 2 coins.
quiz.mistake: Does not start with the biggest coin

quiz.q: Which matches a ₹20 note?

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to carry ₹6 with as few coins as I can. Which coins should I take?
teach.praise: ₹5 and ₹1. Only 2 coins! Light wings!
teach.nudge: Which is the biggest coin that fits in ₹6?

learn.hook: Clink! Clink! Coins go into the piggy bank. Let us save!
points: Saving means keeping some money for later.
A piggy bank keeps our coins safe.
Add each coin you put in to know how much you have saved.
Saving a little every day adds up to a lot!

example.q: Monday ₹5, Tuesday ₹2, Wednesday ₹2 go in the piggy bank. How much is saved?

learn.reallife: Many children save coins for a book, a toy or a gift for someone they love.

games.title: True or false?
items: Saving money is a good habit.
It helps us buy things we need later.
A piggy bank keeps coins safe.
Coins stay inside until we need them.
If we save ₹1 a day for 5 days, we save ₹5.
We should spend all our money at once.
Saving some helps us buy bigger things later.

quiz.q: Joseph puts ₹2, ₹5 and ₹1 in his piggy bank. How much has he saved?
Riya saves ₹2 every day for 5 days. How much does she save?
Why do we save money?
options: To buy something we need later
quiz.explain: Saved money can be used later for something useful.
quiz.mistake: Does not know why saving helps

quiz.q: Kabir's piggy bank has ₹10 + ₹10 + ₹5. How much is in it?
Aisha wants a ₹20 book. She has saved ₹15. How much more must she save?
quiz.mistake: Adds the price and the savings

quiz.q: Which is a good saving habit?
options: Put a coin in the piggy bank each week
quiz.explain: Saving a little often adds up.
quiz.mistake: Does not see what saving means

teach.ask: Gappu: Why should I put my coins in a piggy bank? How do I know how much I saved?
teach.praise: Saving keeps coins safe for later. Add them up to know your total!
teach.nudge: What is a piggy bank for? How do I find the total?

learn.hook: Kabir's toys are all mixed up! Let us sort them.
points: Sorting means putting things that are alike together.
We can sort by colour, shape, size or kind.
Each group shares something the same.
The same toys can be sorted in different ways.

example.q: Sort: 🚗 🧸 🚌 🪁 🚲. Which toys move on wheels?

learn.reallife: We sort clothes in a cupboard, spoons in a drawer and books on a shelf.

quiz.q: Which one does NOT belong? 🍎 🍌 🚗 🍇
quiz.explain: 🍎, 🍌 and 🍇 are fruits. 🚗 is a car.
quiz.mistake: Does not see what the group has in common

quiz.q: Riya sorts by colour. Where does a red ball go?
quiz.explain: She is sorting by colour, so red goes with red.
quiz.mistake: Uses a different rule than the one given

quiz.q: Which is a good way to sort crayons?
quiz.explain: Crayons have different colours. Colour is easy to see.
quiz.mistake: Picks a rule that does not fit

quiz.q: What is the same in 🔺 🔺 🔺?
quiz.explain: All three are triangles. They have the same shape.
quiz.mistake: Looks at something that is not shown

quiz.q: Which toy does NOT belong? ⚽ 🏀 🎾 🧸
quiz.explain: ⚽, 🏀 and 🎾 are balls. 🧸 is a teddy.
quiz.mistake: Picks an item that fits the group

quiz.q: Arjun puts 🚗 🚌 🚲 together. What rule did he use?
quiz.explain: A car, a bus and a cycle all have wheels.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the common feature

teach.ask: Gappu: My toy box is a mess! How do I sort it?
teach.praise: Put the same kind together. Now my box is neat!
teach.nudge: What should go together? By colour or by kind?

learn.hook: After sorting, we can count each group!
points: Sort the things first.
Count each group.
Then we can see which group has the most.
We can also find how many in all.

example.q: 🚗🚗🚗 🧸🧸 ⚽⚽⚽⚽. Which group has the most?

learn.reallife: A teacher counts how many children bring tiffin and how many buy lunch.

quiz.q: 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍌🍌. How many apples?
quiz.explain: Count only the apples: 1, 2, 3, 4.

quiz.q: 🧸🧸🚗🚗🚗🚗🚗. Are there more teddies or cars?
quiz.explain: Cars: 5. Teddies: 2. 5 is more.

quiz.q: ⚽⚽⚽ 🏀🏀. How many balls in all?
Meena has 6 dolls and 4 blocks. How many more dolls than blocks?
🎈🎈🎈 🪁🪁🪁. What is true?
quiz.explain: 3 balloons and 3 kites. They are the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one group must be bigger

quiz.q: 🐶🐶 🐱🐱🐱 🐰. Which group has the fewest?
quiz.explain: Dogs: 2. Cats: 3. Rabbit: 1. 1 is the fewest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the most instead of the fewest

teach.ask: Gappu: There are cars and teddies all mixed up. Which is more?
teach.praise: Sort them, count each group, then compare. Easy!
teach.nudge: Should I sort them first? Then what do I do?

learn.hook: A picture graph shows counts with little pictures!
points: Each picture stands for one thing.
A row with more pictures means more things.
We count the pictures in each row.
We can see the most and the least quickly.

example.q: Toys in class: Cars 🚗🚗🚗🚗, Balls ⚽⚽, Dolls 🪆🪆🪆. Which toy is the most?

learn.reallife: Teachers make picture graphs of favourite fruits or how children come to school.

games.title: Read the graph: 🍎🍎🍎 apples, 🍌🍌🍌🍌🍌 bananas, 🥭🥭 mangoes
items: Only 2 mangoes. That is the least.
There are more apples than bananas.

games.title: Fill from the graph: 🚌 🚌 🚌 bus, 🚲 🚲 cycle, 🚶 🚶 🚶 🚶 walk

quiz.q: Favourite sweets: Laddoo 🟡🟡🟡🟡, Jalebi 🟠🟠, Barfi ⚪⚪⚪. Which is liked most?
quiz.explain: Laddoo has 4 pictures. That is the most.

quiz.q: Pets: Dogs 🐶🐶🐶, Cats 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟🐟🐟. How many fish?
quiz.explain: Count the fish row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

quiz.q: Pets: Dogs 🐶🐶🐶, Cats 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟🐟🐟. Which pet is the least?
quiz.explain: Cats have only 2 pictures. That is the least.

quiz.q: Kites: Riya 🪁🪁🪁, Arjun 🪁🪁🪁🪁🪁🪁. How many more does Arjun have?
Fruits: 🍎🍎 apples, 🍌🍌🍌 bananas, 🍇🍇🍇🍇 grapes. How many fruits in all?
In a picture graph, what does one 🌸 show?
quiz.explain: In our graphs, each picture stands for one thing.

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a picture graph? How do I read it?
teach.praise: Count the pictures in each row. The longest row has the most!
teach.nudge: What does each picture show? How do I find the most?

learn.hook: So many flowers! How can we remember how many of each colour?
points: Count the flowers of each colour.
Make a mark | for each flower. Every 5 marks, start a new group.
Write the counts in a table: colour on one side, number on the other.
Use the table to say true or false: 'There are more red than yellow.'

example.q: Red flowers: ||||. Yellow flowers: ||||| ||. Which colour has more? Write the counts.

learn.reallife: Teachers keep a record of who is present with a tick for each child.

games.title: Read the table: Red 6, Yellow 4, Pink 6
items: There are more red than yellow flowers.
Pink has fewer flowers than yellow.

quiz.q: Riya counts white flowers: ||||| |||. How many?
quiz.explain: 5 marks and 3 more make 8.

quiz.q: Table: Red 5, Blue 3. Is 'There are more blue than red' true?
quiz.explain: Red has 5. Blue has 3. Red has more.
quiz.mistake: Reads the table the wrong way round

quiz.q: Kabir sees 6 pink flowers. How many marks should he draw?
quiz.explain: One mark for each flower: 6 marks.

quiz.q: Table: Red 4, Yellow 7, White 2. How many flowers in all?
Table: Orange 3, Purple 3. What is true?
quiz.explain: Both are 3.

quiz.q: Why do we write counts in a table?
options: To remember and compare them easily
quiz.explain: A table keeps all the counts in one place.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why we record data

teach.ask: Gappu: I counted 4 red flowers and 6 yellow ones. How do I write it down so I don't forget?
teach.praise: 4 marks for red, 6 for yellow, in a table. Yellow has more!
teach.nudge: How can I show each flower on paper?

learn.hook: Hide, look, remember! Can you find the hidden numbers?
points: Memory game: number cards are hidden under bowls. Look, remember, then say which card is where.
In a tricky picture, count slowly. Touch or mark each thing once.
For a stack of logs, count row by row.
A puzzle may hide the numbers 1 to 10. Tick each one as you find it.

example.q: A stack of logs has 3 at the bottom, 2 in the middle and 1 on top. How many logs?
steps: Count row by row: 3, then 2, then 1.

learn.reallife: When we pack school bags, we count books carefully so nothing is left behind.

games.title: Find the hidden numbers
games.prompt: Tick them from 1 to 10 in order

games.title: True or false?
items: Otherwise the count will be wrong.
In a memory game, guessing is better than remembering.
Counting row by row helps in a tricky picture.
Then we do not miss any.
If 1, 2, 3, 5 are found, 4 is still hiding.

quiz.q: Bowls hide cards 3, 7 and 1 from left to right. Which card is under the middle bowl?
quiz.explain: Left 3, middle 7, right 1.

quiz.q: Logs: 4 at the bottom, 3 in the middle, 2 on top. How many logs?
Riya found 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 in a puzzle. Which number is still hiding?
quiz.explain: Count 1 to 10. 5 is missing.

quiz.q: Bowls hide cards 2, 9, 4, 6. Kabir lifts the last bowl. Which card will he see?
quiz.explain: The last card is 6.

quiz.q: Aisha counted a heap of bangles twice and got two different numbers. What should she do?
options: Count again slowly, touching each one
quiz.explain: Careful, slow counting gives the right answer.

quiz.q: Which numbers are missing from 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10?
quiz.explain: Count 1 to 10. 3 and 7 are not there.

teach.ask: Gappu: My stack has 3 sticks at the bottom, 2 above, and 1 on top. How do I count without mistakes?
teach.praise: Row by row: 3, 2, 1. That is 6. No mistakes!
teach.nudge: Should I count every stick? How many in each row?

topics.title: Who am I? Mirror and matchstick numbers

learn.hook: I am a number with a secret. Use the clues to find me!
points: 'Who am I?' riddles give clues: 'I come just after 19.' Answer: 20.
Clues can use tens and ones: 'I have 2 tens and 5 ones.' Answer: 25.
A mirror flips a number from left to right. 18 in a mirror shows the 8 on the left, flipped.
Numbers can be made with matchsticks, like on a digital clock. 1 needs 2 sticks. 8 needs 7 sticks.
Moving one stick can change a number: 6 can become 9.

example.q: Who am I? I am between 34 and 36.

learn.reallife: Digital clocks and lift buttons show numbers made of little lines, like matchsticks.

games.title: True or false?
items: A mirror flips numbers from left to right.
Left goes to right and right to left.
In digital-clock style, 1 is made with 2 matchsticks.
Two sticks stand one above the other.
In digital-clock style, 8 needs fewer sticks than 1.
Moving one stick can change 6 into 9.
Move the bottom-left stick to the top-right.

quiz.q: Who am I? I come just after 29.
quiz.explain: 1 more than 29 is 30.

quiz.q: Who am I? I have 4 tens and 3 ones.
Who am I? I am 1 less than 60.
quiz.explain: 1 less than 60 is 59.

quiz.q: Kabir holds the card 18 up to a mirror. Which digit is on the left in the mirror?
quiz.explain: A mirror swaps left and right, so the 8 moves to the left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a mirror keeps the order

quiz.q: In digital-clock style, how many matchsticks make the number 1?
quiz.explain: On a digital clock, 1 is made of 2 sticks, one above the other.

quiz.q: Which number can 6 become by moving just one matchstick?
quiz.explain: Move the bottom-left stick to the top-right and 6 becomes 9.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that needs fewer sticks

teach.ask: Gappu: Who am I? I have 1 ten and 6 ones.
teach.praise: 10 and 6 make 16. You found me!
teach.nudge: How much is 1 ten? Add the ones.

learn.hook: One answer, many questions! Let us play with sums.
points: Equal sides puzzle: put 1 to 5 in two lines that share the middle box. Both lines must have the same sum.
With 5 in the middle: 1, 5, 4 and 2, 5, 3. Both make 10.
Many questions have the answer 8: 4 + 4, 5 + 3, 10 - 2.
17 can be made in many ways: 10 + 7, 9 + 8, 12 + 5.

example.q: Two lines share the middle box with 3 in it. Line one is 1, 3, 5. Line two is 2, 3, ___. Use 1 to 5 once each.

learn.reallife: There are many ways to share sweets so that two friends get the same.

quiz.q: Middle box is 5. Line one is 1, 5, 4. Line two is 2, 5, ___. Which number makes both lines equal?
Middle box is 1. Line one is 2, 1, 5. Line two is 3, 1, ___. Which number makes both lines equal?
Which question has the answer 8?
quiz.mistake: Does not work out each one

quiz.q: Which pair adds up to 17?
quiz.explain: 9 + 8 = 17. The others make 16.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a way to make 17?

teach.ask: Gappu: Can you tell me three different questions whose answer is 8?
teach.praise: So many ways to make 8! You are a puzzle star!
teach.nudge: Can I add two numbers to get 8? Can I take away to get 8?

topics.title: Take away again; magic cross; centre numbers

learn.hook: Take away, take away, take away... until nothing is left!
points: How many times can 5 be taken from 25? 25, 20, 15, 10, 5, 0. That is 5 times.
Magic cross: put 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 in a row and a column that share the centre box. Both must have the same total.
With 7 in the centre: row 5, 7, 9 and column 6, 7, 8. Both make 21.
Centre puzzle: the centre number comes from the numbers around it. Find the rule, like 'add them'.

example.q: How many times can you take 5 away from 15?

learn.reallife: Sharing 20 laddoos, 5 at a time, until the box is empty is taking away again and again.

games.title: Magic cross with 7 in the centre

quiz.q: How many times can 5 be taken away from 25?
How many times can 2 be taken away from 10?
quiz.explain: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0. That is 5 times.

quiz.q: Magic cross, centre 7. Row: 5, 7, 9. Column: 6, 7, ___. Which number makes both totals equal?
Magic cross, centre 7. What is the total of each line?
Rule: centre = top + bottom. Top is 6, bottom is 3. What is the centre?
Rule: centre = big number - small number. The numbers are 9 and 4. What is the centre?

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 20 seeds. I eat 5 at a time. How many times can I eat until none are left?
teach.praise: 20, 15, 10, 5, 0. Four times! Burp!
teach.nudge: What is left after each time I eat 5?

learn.hook: Pick 3 balls and add the numbers! Can you hit the target?
points: Ball game: balls have numbers 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8. Pick any 3 balls and add.
Highest score: pick the 3 biggest: 8 + 6 + 5 = 19.
Lowest score: pick the 3 smallest: 2 + 4 + 5 = 11.
Fruit puzzle: if 🍎 + 🍎 = 10, then each 🍎 stands for 5.

example.q: Balls: 2, 4, 5, 6, 8. Pick 3 balls to make 12.

learn.reallife: In a fair game, children add their scores to see who wins.

quiz.q: Balls: 2, 4, 5, 6, 8. What is the highest score with 3 balls?
quiz.explain: Pick the 3 biggest: 8 + 6 + 5 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Does not pick the biggest balls

quiz.q: Balls: 2, 4, 5, 6, 8. What is the lowest score with 3 balls?
quiz.explain: Pick the 3 smallest: 2 + 4 + 5 = 11.

quiz.q: Which 3 balls make 12?
quiz.explain: 2 + 4 + 6 = 12. The others make 13 and 17.

quiz.q: 🍎 + 🍎 = 10. What is 🍎?
quiz.mistake: Thinks one apple is the whole 10
Divides into the wrong number of parts

quiz.q: 🍎 = 5 and 🍌 = 3. What is 🍎 + 🍌?

teach.ask: Gappu: 🍐 + 🍐 = 6. What is one 🍐 worth?
teach.praise: 3 + 3 = 6, so 🍐 is 3. Fruit-tastic!
teach.nudge: Two pears are the same. Which number added to itself makes 6?

learn.hook: No repeats allowed! Can you fill the grid?
points: Shape sudoku: each row and each column has every shape once.
In a 3 by 3 grid with 🔺 🟦 ⚪, each row has all three, with no repeats.
Look at what is already in the row and the column. Put in the missing one.
With 4 objects like 🍎 🍌 🍇 🥭, each row and column has all four.
There can be more than one way to fill a grid. Try another!

example.q: Row: 🔺 🟦 ___. Each row has 🔺, 🟦 and ⚪ once. What goes in the gap?

learn.reallife: Sudoku puzzles in newspapers use numbers instead of shapes.

games.title: True or false?
items: In shape sudoku, a row can have two 🔺.
Each shape comes only once in a row.
Each column must have every shape once.
No repeats in a column too.
There can be more than one way to fill an empty grid.
A 4 by 4 grid needs 4 different objects.

quiz.q: Row: ⚪ 🔺 ___. Use 🔺, 🟦, ⚪ once each. What goes in the gap?
quiz.explain: ⚪ and 🔺 are there. 🟦 is missing.
quiz.mistake: Repeats a shape in the row

quiz.q: Column: 🟦 ___ 🔺. Use 🔺, 🟦, ⚪ once each. What goes in the gap?
quiz.explain: 🟦 and 🔺 are there. ⚪ is missing.
quiz.mistake: Repeats a shape in the column

quiz.q: Which row is correct?
quiz.explain: Each shape comes once.

quiz.q: Fruit row: 🍌 ___ 🥭 🍎. Each of 🍎 🍌 🍇 🥭 comes once. Which fruit is missing?
quiz.explain: 🍌, 🥭 and 🍎 are there. 🍇 is missing.

quiz.q: In a 3 by 3 shape sudoku, how many 🔺 are there in all?
quiz.explain: One 🔺 in each of the 3 rows: 3.

quiz.q: Meena filled a grid one way. Can Kabir fill the same empty grid another way?
options: Yes, there can be more than one way
quiz.explain: Different first rows can still follow the rule.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a puzzle has only one answer

teach.ask: Gappu: My row has 🍎 🍇 🥭. I must use 🍎 🍌 🍇 🥭 once each. What is missing?
teach.praise: 🍌 is missing! No repeats now. Well done!
teach.nudge: Which fruit is not in the row yet?

learn.hook: Stack, fit and match! Puzzles with shapes and patterns.
points: Glasses can be stacked like a pyramid: 1 on top, 2 below, 3 below that.
Each new row has 1 more glass than the row above.
A missing piece must match the shape of the gap and the pattern around it.
A shadow has the same outline as the object.

example.q: A glass pyramid has rows of 1, 2 and 3 glasses. Add one more row below. How many glasses in the new row?
steps: Each row has 1 more than the one above.
The last row has 3, so the new row has 4.

learn.reallife: In the evening, your shadow has your shape, with arms, legs and head!

quiz.q: A pyramid has rows of 1, 2 and 3 glasses. How many glasses in all?
Rows go 1, 2, 3, 4 glasses. How many glasses in the next row?
quiz.explain: Each row has 1 more: 4 + 1 = 5.

quiz.q: Glasses go up, down, up, down. What comes next?
quiz.explain: The core is up, down. After down comes up.

quiz.q: A pot has a missing piece. The gap is a triangle with stripes around it. Which piece fits?
quiz.explain: The piece must have the same shape and the same pattern.
quiz.mistake: Matches only colour or only shape

quiz.q: Which shadow belongs to a ball?
quiz.explain: A ball is round, so its shadow is round.

quiz.q: Which object has a rectangle shadow?
quiz.explain: A book has straight sides like a rectangle.

teach.ask: Gappu: My glass pyramid has rows of 1, 2 and 3. What comes next, and how many glasses in all?
teach.praise: Next row has 4, so 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 glasses! Tall tower!
teach.nudge: How many more glasses does each new row get?

learn.hook: ₹49 with as few coins and notes as possible. Can you crack it?
points: We have ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20 coins and notes.
Start with the biggest one that fits. Then the next biggest.

example.q: Make ₹27 with the fewest coins and notes.

learn.reallife: Cashiers give change using big notes first, so they hand over fewer pieces.

quiz.q: What is the fewest coins and notes to make ₹49?
quiz.mistake: Does not start with the biggest

quiz.q: After two ₹20 notes, how much more is needed to make ₹49?
Make ₹9 with the fewest coins. Which coins?
quiz.explain: 5 + 2 + 2 = 9 with only 3 coins.
quiz.mistake: Uses more small coins than needed

quiz.q: Make ₹32 with the fewest pieces. How many pieces?
Which is the biggest note to start with for ₹35?
quiz.explain: ₹20 is the biggest that fits in ₹35.

quiz.q: Riya makes ₹49 with ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹5 + ₹2 + ₹2. Check: what is the total?

teach.ask: Gappu: I need ₹45. Which coins and notes should I take so I carry the fewest?
teach.praise: ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹5. Only 3 pieces! Light and quick!
teach.nudge: What is the biggest note that fits? Then what is left?
